<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM 1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">OUR BUSINESS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Introduction</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1932.&#160;&#160;The Company owns and operates assets in the regulated and unregulated natural gas industry and is primarily engaged in the gathering, processing, transportation, storage and distribution of natural gas in the United States.&#160;&#160;The Company operates in three reportable segments:&#160;&#160;Transportation and Storage, Gathering and Processing, and Distribution.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">BUSINESS SEGMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Reportable Segments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s operations, as reported, include three reportable segments:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div>

</td>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has other operations that support and expand its natural gas and other energy sales, which are not included in its reportable segments.&#160;&#160;These operations do not meet the quantitative thresholds for determining reportable segments and have been combined for disclosure purposes in the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Corporate and Other activities</font> category.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For information about the revenues, EBIT, earnings from unconsolidated investments, operating income, assets and other financial information relating to reportable segments and the Corporate and Other activities, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 7. <div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company also provides various corporate services to support its operating businesses, including executive management, accounting, communications, human resources, information technology, insurance, internal audit, investor relations, environmental, legal, payroll, purchasing, insurance, tax and treasury.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales of products or services between segments are billed at regulated rates or at market rates, as applicable.&#160;&#160;There were no material intersegment revenues.</font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Transportation and Storage Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Services</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Transportation and Storage segment is primarily engaged in the interstate transportation of natural gas to Midwest, Southwest and Florida markets and related storage, and also provides LNG terminalling and regasification services.&#160;&#160;The Transportation and Storage segment&#8217;s operations are conducted through Panhandle and Citrus.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Panhandle.</font>&#160;&#160;Panhandle owns and operates a large natural gas open-access interstate pipeline network.&#160;&#160;The pipeline network, consisting of the PEPL, Trunkline and Sea Robin transmission systems, serves customers in the Midwest, Gulf Coast and Midcontinent United States with a comprehensive array of transportation and storage services.&#160;&#160;PEPL&#8217;s transmission system consists of four large diameter pipelines extending approximately 1,300 miles from producing areas in the Anadarko Basin of Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas through Missouri, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio and into Michigan.&#160;&#160;Trunkline&#8217;s transmission system consists of two large diameter pipelines extending approximately 1,400 miles from the Gulf Coast areas of Texas and Louisiana through Arkansas, Mississippi, Tennessee, Kentucky, Illinois, Indiana and to Michigan.&#160;&#160;Sea Robin&#8217;s transmission system consists of two offshore Louisiana natural gas supply systems extending approximately 81 miles into the Gulf of Mexico. In connection with its natural gas pipeline transmission and storage systems, Panhandle has five natural gas storage fields located in Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan and Oklahoma.&#160;&#160;Southwest Gas operates four of these fields and Trunkline operates one.&#160;&#160;Through Trunkline LNG, Panhandle owns and operates an LNG terminal in Lake Charles, Louisiana.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Panhandle earns most of its revenue by entering into firm transportation and storage contracts, providing capacity for customers to transport and store natural gas, or LNG, in its facilities.&#160;&#160;Panhandle provides firm transportation services under contractual arrangements to local distribution company customers and their affiliates, natural gas marketers, producers, other pipelines, electric power generators and a variety of end-users.&#160;&#160;Panhandle&#8217;s pipelines offer both firm and interruptible transportation to customers on a short-term and long-term basis.&#160;&#160;Demand for natural gas transmission on Panhandle&#8217;s pipeline systems peaks during the winter months, with the highest throughput and a higher portion of annual total operating revenues and EBIT occurring during the first and fourth calendar quarters.&#160;&#160;Average reservation revenue rates realized by Panhandle are dependent on certain factors, including but not limited to rate regulation, customer demand for capacity, and capacity sold for a given period and, in some cases, utilization of capacity.&#160;&#160;Commodity or utilization revenues, which are more variable in nature, are dependent upon a number of factors including weather, storage levels and pipeline capacity availability levels, and customer demand for firm and interruptible services, including parking services.&#160;&#160;The majority of Panhandle&#8217;s revenues are related to firm capacity reservation charges, which reservation charges accounted for approximately 88 percent of total segment revenues and 27 percent of consolidated revenues in 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Florida Gas.&#160;&#160;</font>Florida Gas is an open-access interstate pipeline system with a mainline capacity of 2.3 Bcf/d and approximately 5,000 miles of pipelines extending from south Texas through the Gulf Coast region of the United States to south Florida. Florida Gas&#8217; pipeline system primarily receives natural gas from natural gas producing basins along the Louisiana and Texas Gulf Coast, Mobile Bay and offshore Gulf of Mexico.&#160;&#160;Florida Gas is the principal transporter of natural gas to the Florida energy market, delivering over 63 percent of the natural gas consumed in the state.&#160;&#160;In addition, Florida Gas&#8217; pipeline system operates and maintains over 60 interconnects with major interstate and intrastate natural gas pipelines, which provide Florida Gas&#8217; customers access to diverse natural gas producing regions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Florida Gas earns the majority of its revenue through firm transportation contracts.&#160;&#160;&#160;Florida Gas also earns variable revenue from charges assessed on each unit of transportation provided.</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Demand for natural gas transmission service on the Florida Gas pipeline system is somewhat seasonal, with the highest throughput and related net earnings occurring in the traditional summer cooling season during the second and third calendar quarters, primarily due to increased natural gas-fired electric generation loads.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s share of net earnings of Florida Gas is reported in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Earnings from unconsolidated investments</font> in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Recent System Enhancements &#8211; Completed or Under Construction</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">LNG Terminal Enhancement.</font>&#160;&#160;Trunkline LNG commenced construction of an enhancement at its LNG terminal in February 2007.&#160;&#160;The key components of the enhancement were an ambient air vaporizer system and NGL recovery units.&#160;&#160;On March 11, 2010, Trunkline LNG received approval from FERC to place the infrastructure enhancement construction project in service.&#160;&#160;Total construction costs were approximately $440 million plus capitalized interest.&#160;&#160;The negotiated rate with the project&#8217;s customer, BG LNG Services, will be adjusted based on final capital costs pursuant to a contract-based formula.&#160;&#160;In addition, Trunkline LNG and BG LNG Services have extended the existing terminal and pipeline services agreements to coincide with the infrastructure enhancement construction project contract, which runs 20 years from the in-service date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Florida Gas Phase VIII Expansion</font>.&#160; In November 2009, FERC approved Florida Gas&#8217; certificate application to construct an expansion, which will increase its natural gas capacity into Florida by approximately 820 MMcf/d (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Phase VIII Expansion</font>).&#160; Florida Gas anticipates an in-service date in April 2011, at a currently estimated cost of approximately $2.48 billion, including capitalized equity and debt costs.&#160;&#160;Approximately $2.2 billion of capital costs have been recorded as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;To date, Florida Gas has entered into firm transportation service agreements with shippers for 25-year terms accounting for approximately 74 percent of the available expansion capacity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Panhandle and Florida Gas are subject to regulation by various federal, state and local governmental agencies, including those specifically described below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FERC has comprehensive jurisdiction over Panhandle and Florida Gas.&#160;&#160;In accordance with the Natural Gas Act of 1938, FERC&#8217;s jurisdiction over natural gas companies encompasses, among other things, the acquisition, operation and disposition of assets and facilities, the services provided and rates charged.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FERC has authority to regulate rates and charges for transportation and storage of natural gas in interstate commerce.&#160;&#160;FERC also has authority over the construction and operation of pipeline and related facilities utilized in the transportation and sale of natural gas in interstate commerce, including the extension, enlargement or abandonment of service using such facilities.&#160;&#160;PEPL, Trunkline, Sea Robin, Trunkline LNG, Southwest Gas and Florida Gas hold certificates of public convenience and necessity issued by FERC, authorizing them to operate the pipelines, facilities and properties now in operation and to transport and store natural gas in interstate commerce.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For additional information regarding Panhandle and Florida Gas&#8217; regulation and rates, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 1A.&#160;&#160;Risk Factors &#8211; Risks That Relate to the Company&#8217;s Transportation and Storage Segment</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 5 &#8211; Unconsolidated Investments &#8211; Contingent Matters Potentially Impacting Southern Union Through the Company&#8217;s Investment in Citrus &#8211; Florida Gas Rate Filing </font>and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates &#8211; Panhandle.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The interstate pipeline systems of Panhandle and Florida Gas compete with those of other interstate and intrastate pipeline companies in the transportation and storage of natural gas.&#160;&#160;The principal elements of competition among pipelines are rates, terms of service, flexibility and reliability of service.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Natural gas competes with other forms of energy available to the Company&#8217;s customers and end-users, including electricity, coal and fuel oils.&#160;&#160;The primary competitive factor is price.&#160;&#160;Changes in the availability or price of natural gas and other forms of energy, the level of business activity, conservation, legislation and governmental regulation, the capability to convert to alternate fuels and other factors, including weather and natural gas storage levels, affect the ongoing demand for natural gas in the areas served by Panhandle and Florida Gas.&#160;&#160;In order to meet these challenges, Panhandle and Florida Gas will need to adapt their marketing strategies, the types of transportation and storage services provided and their pricing and rates to address competitive forces.&#160;&#160;In addition, FERC may authorize the construction of new interstate pipelines that compete with the Company&#8217;s existing pipelines.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Panhandle&#8217;s current direct competitors include Alliance Pipeline LP, ANR Pipeline Company, Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America, ONEOK Partners, Texas Gas Transmission Corporation, Northern Natural Gas Company, Vector Pipeline, Columbia Gulf Transmission, Rockies Express Pipeline and Midwestern Gas Transmission.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Florida Gas competes in peninsular Florida with Gulfstream Natural Gas System, L.L.C., a joint venture of Spectra Energy Corporation and The Williams Companies. Florida Gas also serves the Florida panhandle, where it competes with Gulf South Pipeline Company, LP and the natural gas transportation business of Southern Natural Gas. Florida Gas faces competition, to a lesser degree, from alternate fuels, including residual fuel oil, in the Florida market, as well as from proposed LNG regasification facilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gathering and Processing Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Services</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS&#8217; operations consist of a network of natural gas and NGL pipelines, four cryogenic processing plants and five natural gas treating plants.&#160;&#160;The principal assets of SUGS are located in the Permian Basin of Texas and New Mexico.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS is primarily engaged in connecting producing wells of exploration and production (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">E&amp;P</font>) companies to its gathering system, providing compression and gathering services, treating natural gas to remove impurities to meet pipeline quality specifications, processing natural gas for the removal of NGL, and redelivering natural gas and NGL to a variety of markets.&#160;&#160;SUGS&#8217; natural gas supply contracts primarily include fee-based, percent-of-proceeds, and margin sharing contracts (conditioning fee and wellhead purchase contracts).&#160;&#160;SUGS&#8217; primary sales customers include E&amp;P companies, power generating companies, electric and natural gas utilities, energy marketers, industrial end-users located primarily in the Gulf Coast and southwestern United States, and petrochemicals.&#160;&#160;SUGS&#8217; business is not generally seasonal in nature.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of the operational flexibility built into SUGS&#8217; gathering systems and plants, it is able to offer a broad array of services to producers, including:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas and NGL Connections</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS&#8217; major natural gas pipeline interconnects are with ATMOS Pipeline Texas, El Paso Natural Gas Company, Energy Transfer Fuel, Enterprise Texas Pipeline, Northern Natural Gas Company, Oasis Pipeline, ONEOK Westex Transmission, Public Service Company of New Mexico and Transwestern Pipeline Company.&#160;&#160;Its major NGL pipeline interconnects are with Chaparral Energy, Louis Dreyfus Energy Services and Chevron Natural Gas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas Supply Contracts</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS&#8217; natural gas supply contracts primarily include fee-based, percent-of-proceeds, and margin sharing contracts (conditioning fee and wellhead purchase contracts) which, as of December 31, 2010, comprised 13 percent, 68 percent and 19 percent by volume of its natural gas supply contracts, respectively.&#160;&#160;These natural gas supply contracts vary in length from month-to-month to a number of years, with many of the contracts having a term of three to five years.&#160;&#160;Additionally, some contracts contain a combination of these contractual types of structure (e.g., percent-of-proceeds contractual structure combined with a treating fee component).&#160;&#160;Following is a summary description of the natural gas supply contracts utilized by SUGS:</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">9</font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fee-Based.</font>&#160;&#160;Under fee-based arrangements, SUGS receives a fee or fees for one or more of the following services:&#160;&#160;gathering, compressing, dehydrating, treating or processing natural gas.&#160;&#160;The fee or fees are usually based on the volume or level of service provided to gather, compress, dehydrate, treat or process natural gas.&#160;&#160;While fee-based arrangements are generally not subject to commodity risk, certain operating conditions as well as certain provisions of these arrangements, including fuel recovery mechanisms, may subject SUGS to a limited amount of commodity risk.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Percent-of-Proceeds, Percent-of-Value or Percent-of-Liquids.</font>&#160;&#160;Under percent-of-proceeds arrangements, SUGS generally gathers, treats and processes natural gas for producers for an agreed percentage of the proceeds from the sales of residual natural gas and NGL.&#160;&#160;The percent-of-value and percent-of-liquids arrangements are variations on the percent-of-proceeds structure.&#160;&#160;These types of arrangements expose SUGS to significant commodity price risk as the revenues derived from the contracts are directly related to natural gas and NGL prices.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Conditioning Fee.</font>&#160;&#160;Conditioning fee arrangements provide a guaranteed minimum unit margin or fee on natural gas that must be processed for NGL extraction in order to meet the quality specifications of the natural gas transmission pipelines.&#160;&#160;In addition to the minimum unit margin or fee, SUGS retains a significant percentage of the processing spread, if any.&#160;&#160;While the revenue earned is directly related to the processing spread, SUGS is guaranteed a positive margin with a minimum unit margin or fee in low processing spread environments.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 18pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Keep-Whole and Wellhead.&#160;&#160;</font>A keep-whole arrangement allows SUGS to keep 100 percent of the NGL produced, but requires the return of the Btu or dollar value of the underlying natural gas to the producer or owner.&#160;&#160;Since some of the natural gas is converted to NGL during processing, resulting in Btu shrinkage, SUGS must compensate the producer or owner for the Btu shrinkage by replacing the shrinkage in-kind or by paying an agreed, market-based value for the Btu shrinkage.&#160;&#160;These arrangements have the highest commodity price exposure for SUGS because the costs are dependent on the price of natural gas and the revenues are based on the price of NGL.&#160;&#160;As a result, SUGS benefits from these types of arrangements when the Btu value of the NGL is high relative to the Btu value of the natural gas and is disadvantaged when the Btu value of the natural gas is high relative to the Btu value of NGL.&#160;&#160;Rather than incurring negative margins during an unfavorable processing spread environment, SUGS may have the ability to reduce its exposure to negative processing spreads by (i) treating, dehydrating and blending the wellhead natural gas with leaner natural gas in order to meet downstream transmission pipeline specifications rather than processing the natural gas or (ii) reducing the volume of ethane recovered at the processing facility.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas Sales Contracts</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS&#8217; natural gas sales contracts (physical) are consummated under North American Energy Standards Board or Gas Industry Standards Board contracts.&#160;&#160;Pricing is predominately based on Platt&#8217;s Gas Daily at El Paso-Permian or Waha pricing points.&#160;&#160;Some monthly baseload sales are made using FERC (Platt&#8217;s) pricing at El Paso-Permian or Waha pricing points.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NGL Sales Contracts</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS has contracted to sell its entire owned or controlled output of NGL to Conoco Phillips Company (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Conoco</font>) through December 31, 2014.&#160;&#160;Pricing for the NGL volumes sold to Conoco throughout the contract period are based on OPIS pricing at Mont Belvieu, Texas delivery points.&#160;&#160;SUGS has an option to extend the sales agreement for an additional five year period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For information related to SUGS&#8217; use of various derivative financial instruments to manage its commodity price risk and related operating cash flows, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 10 &#8211; Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities &#8211; Gathering and Processing Segment.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NGL Fractionation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS has a multi-year, firm agreement with Enterprise Products Operations, LLC (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Enterprise</font>) for the fractionation of its NGL.&#160;&#160;Enterprise owns several fractionation facilities in the Gulf coast area.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While FERC does not directly regulate SUGS&#8217; facilities for cost-based ratemaking purposes, SUGS is subject to certain oversight by FERC and various other governmental agencies, primarily with respect to matters of asset integrity, safety and environmental protection.&#160;&#160;The relevant agencies include the EPA and its state counterparts, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration and the U.S. Department of Transportation&#8217;s Office of Pipeline Safety and its state counterparts.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that its operations are in compliance, in all material respects, with applicable safety and environmental statutes and regulations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS competes with other midstream service providers and producer-owned midstream facilities in the Permian Basin.&#160;&#160;SUGS&#8217; direct competitors include Targa Resources Partners LP, DCP Midstream Partners, LP, Enterprise Texas Field Services, Anadarko Petroleum, Atlas Pipeline Partners, LP and Regency Gas Services.&#160;&#160;Industry factors that typically affect SUGS&#8217; ability to compete are:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commodity prices for natural gas and NGL also play a major role in drilling activity on or near SUGS&#8217; gathering and processing systems.&#160;&#160;Generally, lower commodity prices will result in less producer drilling activity and, conversely, higher commodity prices will result in increased producer drilling activity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">SUGS has responded to these industry conditions by positioning and configuring its gathering and processing facilities to offer a broad array of services to accommodate the types and quality of natural gas produced in the region, while many competing systems provide only certain of these services.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Services</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s Distribution segment is primarily engaged in the local distribution of natural gas in Missouri, through its Missouri Gas Energy division, and in Massachusetts, through its New England Gas Company division.&#160;&#160;These utilities serve residential, commercial and industrial customers through local distribution systems.&#160;&#160;The distribution operations in Missouri and Massachusetts are regulated by the MPSC and the MDPU, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Distribution segment&#8217;s operations have historically been sensitive to weather and seasonal in nature, with the primary impact on operating revenues, which include pass through gas purchase costs that are seasonally impacted,&#160;&#160;occurring in the traditional winter heating season during the first and fourth calendar quarters.&#160;&#160;On February 10, 2010, the MPSC issued an order approving continued use of a distribution rate structure that eliminates the impact of weather and conservation for Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s residential margin revenues and related earnings and approving expanded use of that distribution rate structure for Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s small general service customers, effective February 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;Together, Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s residential and small general service customers comprised 99 percent of its total customers and approximately 91 percent of its net operating revenues as of February 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;For additional information related to the new rates, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates &#8211; Missouri Gas Energy.</font></font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Significant Customers</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Distribution segment has no single customer, or group of customers under common control, that accounted for ten percent or more of the Company&#8217;s Distribution segment or the Company&#8217;s total consolidated operating revenues for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas Supply</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The cost and reliability of natural gas service are largely dependent upon the Company's ability to achieve favorable mixes of long-term and short-term natural gas supply agreements and fixed and variable trans&#173;portation con&#173;tracts.&#160;&#160;The Com&#173;pany acquires its natural gas supplies directly.&#160;&#160;The Company has enhanced the reliability of the service provided to its customers by obtaining the ability to dispatch and moni&#173;tor natural gas volumes on a daily, hourly or real-time basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the year ended December 31, 2010, the majority of the natural gas requirements for the utility operations of Missouri Gas Energy were delivered under short- and long-term trans&#173;portation contracts through four major pipeline companies and approximately twenty-one commodity suppliers.&#160;&#160;For this same period, the majority of the natural gas requirements of New England Gas Company were delivered under long-term contracts through five major pipeline companies and contracts with three commodity suppliers.&#160;&#160;These con&#173;tracts have various expira&#173;tion dates ranging from 2011 through 2036.&#160;&#160;Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company also have firm natural gas supply commit&#173;ments under short-term and seasonal arrangements available for all of its service territories.&#160;&#160;Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company hold contract rights to over 17 Bcf and 1 Bcf of storage capacity, respectively, to assist in meeting peak demands.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Like the natural gas industry as a whole, Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company utilize natural gas sales and/or transportation contracts with interruption provisions, by which large volume users purchase natural gas with the understanding that they may be forced to shut down or switch to alternate sources of energy at times when the natural gas is needed by higher priority customers for load management.&#160;&#160;In addition, during times of special supply problems, curtail&#173;ments of deliveries to customers with firm contracts may be made in accordance with guidelines estab&#173;lished by appropriate federal and state regulatory agencies.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation and Rates</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s utility operations are regulated as to rates, operations and other matters by the regulatory commissions of the states in which each operates.&#160;&#160;In Missouri, natural gas rates are established by the MPSC on a system-wide basis.&#160;&#160;In Massachusetts, natural gas rates for New England Gas Company are subject to the regulatory authority of the MDPU.&#160;&#160;For additional information concerning recent state and federal regulatory developments, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company holds non-exclusive franchises with varying expiration dates in all incorporated communities where it is necessary to carry on its business as it is now being conducted.&#160;&#160;Fall River, Massachusetts; Kansas City, Missouri; and St. Joseph, Missouri are the largest cities in which the Company's utility cus&#173;tomers are located.&#160;&#160;The franchise in Kansas City, Missouri expires in 2020.&#160;&#160;The franchises in Fall River, Massachusetts and St. Joseph, Missouri are perpetual. Regulatory authorities establish natural gas service rates so as to permit utilities the opportunity to recover operating, admin&#173;istrative and financing costs, and the opportunity to earn a reasonable return on equity.&#160;&#160;Natural gas costs are billed to cus&#173;tomers through purchased natural gas adjustment clauses, which permit the Company to adjust its sales price as the cost of purchased natural gas changes.&#160;&#160;This is important because the cost of natural gas accounts for a signifi&#173;cant portion of the Company's total ex&#173;penses.&#160;&#160;The <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">appropriate regulatory authority must receive notice of such adjustments prior to billing imple&#173;menta&#173;tion.&#160;&#160;The MPSC allows Missouri Gas Energy to make rate adjustments for purchased natural gas cost changes up to four times per year.&#160;&#160;The MDPU permits New England Gas Company to file for purchased natural gas cost rate adjustments at any time its projected revenues and purchased natural gas costs vary by more than five percent.</font></font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">14</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company supports any service rate changes that it proposes to its regulators using an his&#173;toric test year of operating results adjusted to normal conditions and for any known and measurable revenue or expense changes.&#160;&#160;Because the regula&#173;tory process has certain inherent time delays, rate orders in these jurisdictions may not reflect the operating costs at the time new rates are put into effect.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Except for Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s residential customers and small general service customers, who are billed a fixed monthly charge for services provided and a charge for the amount of natural gas used, the Company&#8217;s monthly customer bills contain a fixed service charge, a usage charge for service to deliver natural gas, and a charge for the amount of natural gas used.&#160;&#160;Although the monthly fixed charge provides an even revenue stream, the usage charge increases the Company's revenue and earnings in the traditional heating load months when usage of natural gas increases.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to public service commission regu&#173;la&#173;tion, the Distribution segment is affected by certain other regula&#173;tions, including pipe&#173;line safety regulations under the Natural Gas Pipeline Safety Act of 1968, the Pipeline Safety Improvement Act of 2002, safety regulations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and various state and federal environmental statutes and regulations.&#160;&#160;The Com&#173;pany believes that its utility operations are in compliance, in all material respects, with applicable safety and environ&#173;mental statutes and regulations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As energy providers, Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company have historic&#173;ally competed with alterna&#173;tive energy sources available to end-users in their service areas, particularly electri&#173;city, propane, fuel oil, coal, NGL and other refined products.&#160;&#160;At present rates, the cost of electricity to residential and com&#173;mer&#173;cial customers in the Com&#173;pany&#8217;s regulated utility ser&#173;vice areas generally is higher than the effective cost of natural gas service.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance, however, that future fluctuations in natural gas and electric costs will not reduce the cost advantage of natural gas service.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Competition from the use of fuel oils and propane, particularly by industrial and electric generation cus&#173;to&#173;mers, has increased due to the volatility of natural gas prices and increased marketing efforts from various energy companies.&#160;&#160;Competition from the use of fuel oils and propane is generally greater in the Company&#8217;s Massachusetts service area than in its Missouri service area. Nevertheless, this competition affects the nationwide market for natural gas.&#160;&#160;Addi&#173;tionally, the general economic conditions in the Company&#8217;s regulated utility service areas continue to affect certain customers and market areas, thus impacting the results of the Company&#8217;s operations.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s regulated utility operations are not currently in significant direct competition with any other distributors of natural gas to residential and small commercial customers within their service areas.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">OTHER MATTERS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Environmental</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is subject to federal, state and local laws and regulations relating to the protection of the environment.&#160;&#160;These evolving laws and regulations may require expenditures over a long period of time to con&#173;trol environmental impacts.&#160;&#160;The Company has established procedures for the ongoing evaluation of its operations to identify potential environmental exposures.&#160;&#160;These procedures are designed to achieve compliance with such laws and regulations.&#160;&#160;For additional information concerning the impact of environmental regulation on the Company, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 1A. Risk Factors </font>and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 14 &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Insurance</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company maintains insurance coverage provided under its policies similar to other comparable companies in the same lines of business.&#160;&#160;This includes, but is not limited to, insurance for potential liability to third parties, worker&#8217;s compensation, automobile and property insurance.&#160;&#160;The insurance policies are subject to terms, conditions, limitations and exclusions that do not fully compensate the Company for all losses.&#160;&#160;Except for windstorm property insurance more fully described below, insurance deductibles range from $100,000 to $10 million for the various policies utilized by the Company.&#160;&#160;As the Company renews its policies, it is possible that some of the current insurance coverage may not be renewed or obtainable on commercially reasonable terms due to restrictive insurance markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Oil Insurance Limited (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">OIL</font>), the&#160;Company&#8217;s member mutual property insurer, revised its windstorm insurance coverage effective January 1, 2010.&#160; Based on the revised coverage,&#160; the per occurrence windstorm claims for onshore and offshore assets are limited to $250 million per member subject to a fixed 60 percent payout, up to $150 million per member, and are subject to the $750 million aggregate limit for total payout to members per incident and a $10 million deductible.&#160;&#160;The revised windstorm coverage also limits annual individual member recovery to $300 million in the aggregate. &#160;The Company has also purchased additional excess insurance coverage for its onshore assets arising from windstorm damage, which provides up to an additional $100 million of property insurance coverage over and above existing coverage or in excess of the base OIL coverage.&#160;&#160;In the event windstorm damage claims are made by the Company for its onshore assets and such damage claims are subject to a scaled or aggregate limit reduction by OIL, the Company may have additional uninsured exposure prior to application of the excess insurance coverage.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM 1A.&#160;&#160;Risk Factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones faced by the Company. Additional risks and uncertainties that the Company is unaware of, or that it currently deems immaterial, may become important factors that affect it. If any of the following risks occurs, the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows could be materially and adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">RISKS THAT RELATE TO SOUTHERN UNION</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Southern Union has substantial debt and may not be able to obtain funding or obtain funding on acceptable terms because of deterioration in the credit and capital markets.&#160;&#160;This may hinder or prevent Southern Union from meeting its future capital needs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Southern Union has a significant amount of debt outstanding.&#160;&#160;As of December&#160;31, 2010, consolidated debt on the Consolidated Balance Sheet totaled $3.52 billion&#160;outstanding, compared to total capitalization (long and short-term debt plus stockholders' equity) of $6.05 billion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Some of the Company&#8217;s debt obligations contain financial covenants concerning debt-to-capital ratios and interest coverage ratios.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s failure to comply with any of these covenants could result in an event of default which, if not cured or waived, could result in the acceleration of outstanding debt obligations or render it unable to borrow under certain credit agreements. Any such acceleration or inability to borrow could cause a material adverse change in the Company&#8217;s financial condition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company relies on access to both short- and long-term credit as a significant source of liquidity for capital requirements not satisfied by the cash flow from its operations.&#160;&#160;A deterioration in the Company&#8217;s financial condition could hamper its ability to access the capital markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Global financial markets and economic conditions have been, and may continue to be, disrupted and volatile.&#160; The current weak economic conditions have made, and may continue to make, obtaining funding more difficult.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Due to these factors, the Company cannot be certain that funding will be available if needed and, to the extent required, on acceptable terms.&#160;&#160;If funding is not available when needed, or is available only on unfavorable terms, the Company may be unable to grow its existing business, complete acquisitions, refinance its debt or otherwise take advantage of business opportunities or respond to competitive pressures, any of which could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s revenues and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Further, because of the need for certain state regulatory approvals in order to incur long-term debt and issue capital stock, the Company may not be able to access the capital markets on a timely basis. Restrictions on the Company&#8217;s ability to access capital markets could affect its ability to execute its business plan or limit its ability to pursue improvements or acquisitions on which it may otherwise rely for future growth.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Credit ratings downgrades could increase the Company&#8217;s financing costs and limit its ability to access the capital markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2010, both Southern Union&#8217;s and Panhandle&#8217;s debt were rated BBB- by Fitch Ratings, Baa3 by Moody's Investor Services, Inc. and BBB- by Standard &amp; Poor's.&#160;&#160;If the Company&#8217;s credit ratings are downgraded below investment grade or if there are times when it is placed on "credit watch," the Company could be negatively impacted as follows:</font></div>

<br>
<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; &#183;&#160; borrowing costs associated with debt obligations could increase annually up to approximately $8.1 million;</font></div>

<div>

</td>

</div>

<div>

</td>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The financial soundness of the Company&#8217;s customers could affect its business and operating results and the Company&#8217;s credit risk management may not be adequate to protect against customer risk.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of the recent disruptions in the financial markets and other macroeconomic challenges that have impacted the economy of the United States and other parts of the world, the Company&#8217;s customers may experience cash flow concerns.&#160;&#160;As a result, if customers&#8217; operating and financial performance deteriorates, or if they are unable to make scheduled payments or obtain credit, customers may not be able to pay, or may delay payment of, accounts receivable owed to the Company.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s credit procedures and policies may not be adequate to fully eliminate customer credit risk.&#160;&#160;In addition, in certain situations, the Company may assume certain additional credit risks for competitive reasons or otherwise.&#160;&#160;Any inability of the Company&#8217;s customers to pay for services could adversely affect the Company&#8217;s financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The Company depends on distributions from its subsidiaries and joint ventures to meet its needs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is dependent on the earnings and cash flows of, and dividends, loans, advances or other distributions from, its subsidiaries to generate the funds necessary to meet its obligations.&#160;&#160;The availability of distributions from such entities is subject to their earnings and capital requirements, the satisfaction of various covenants and conditions contained in financing documents by which they are bound or in their organizational documents, and in the case of the regulated subsidiaries, regulatory restrictions that limit their ability to distribute profits to Southern Union.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><br>
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company owns 50 percent of Citrus, the holding company for Florida Gas.&#160;&#160;As such, the Company cannot control or guarantee the receipt of distributions from Florida Gas through Citrus.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The Company&#8217;s growth strategy entails risk for investors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">These factors could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows, particularly in the case of a larger acquisition or multiple acquisitions in a short period of time.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The consideration paid in connection with an investment or acquisition also affects the Company&#8217;s financial results. To the extent it issues shares of capital stock or other rights to purchase capital stock, including options or other rights, existing stockholders may be diluted and earnings per share may decrease. In addition, acquisitions or expansions may result in the incurrence of additional debt.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The Company is subject to operating risks.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s operations are subject to all operating hazards and risks incident to handling, storing, transporting and providing customers with natural gas or NGL, including adverse weather conditions, explosions, pollution, release of toxic substances, fires and other hazards, each of which could result in damage to or destruction of its facilities or damage to persons and property. If any of these events were to occur, the Company could suffer substantial losses. Moreover, as a result, the Company has been, and likely will be, a defendant in legal proceedings and litigation arising in the ordinary course of business. While the Company maintains insurance against many of these risks to the extent and in amounts that it believes are reasonable, the Company&#8217;s insurance coverages have significant deductibles and self-insurance levels, limits on maximum recovery, and do not cover all risks.&#160;&#160;There is also the risk that the coverages will change over time in light of increased premiums or changes in the terms of the insurance coverages that could result in the Company&#8217;s decision to either terminate certain coverages, increase deductibles and self-insurance levels, or decrease maximum recoveries.&#160;&#160;In addition, there is a risk that the insurers may default on their coverage obligations. As a result, the Company&#8217;s results of operations, cash flows or financial condition could be adversely affected if a significant event occurs that is not fully covered by insurance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Terrorist attacks, such as the attacks that occurred on September&#160;11, 2001, have resulted in increased costs, and the consequences of terrorism may adversely impact the Company&#8217;s results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The impact that terrorist attacks, such as the attacks of September&#160;11, 2001, may have on the energy industry in general, and on the Company in particular, is not known at this time. Uncertainty surrounding military activity may affect the Company&#8217;s operations in unpredictable ways, including disruptions of fuel supplies and markets and the possibility that infrastructure facilities, including pipelines, LNG facilities, gathering facilities and processing plants, could be direct targets of, or indirect casualties of, an act of terror or a retaliatory strike. The Company may have to incur significant additional costs in the future to safeguard its physical assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The success of the pipeline and gathering and processing businesses depends, in part, on factors beyond the Company&#8217;s control.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Third parties own most of the natural gas transported and stored through the pipeline systems operated by Panhandle and Florida Gas.&#160;&#160;Additionally, third parties produce all of the natural gas gathered and processed by SUGS, and third parties provide all of the NGL transportation and fractionation services for SUGS.&#160;&#160;As a result, the volume of natural gas or NGL transported, stored, gathered, processed or fractionated depends on the actions of those third parties and is beyond the Company&#8217;s control.&#160;&#160;Further, other factors beyond the Company&#8217;s and those third parties&#8217; control may unfavorably impact the Company&#8217;s ability to maintain or increase current transmission, storage, gathering or processing rates, to renegotiate existing contracts as they expire or to remarket unsubscribed capacity.&#160;&#160;High utilization of contracted capacity by firm customers reduces capacity available for interruptible transportation and parking services.</font></div>
