<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution Segment.</font>&#160;&#160;The Distribution segment is primarily engaged in the local distribution of natural gas in Missouri and Massachusetts through the Company&#8217;s Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company operating divisions, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Distribution segment&#8217;s operations are regulated by the public utility regulatory commissions of the states in which each operates.&#160;&#160;For information related to the status of current rate filings relating to the Distribution segment, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 1.&#160;&#160;Business &#8211; Business Segments &#8211; Distribution Segment</font>. The Distribution segment&#8217;s operations have historically been sensitive to weather and seasonal in nature, with a significant percentage of annual operating revenues (which include pass through gas purchase costs that are seasonally impacted) and EBIT occurring in the traditional winter heating season during the first and fourth calendar quarters.&#160;&#160;On February 10, 2010, the MPSC issued an order approving continued use of a distribution rate structure that eliminates the impact of weather and conservation for Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s residential margin revenues and related earnings and approving expanded use of that distribution rate structure for Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s small general service customers, effective February 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;Together, Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s residential and small general service customers comprised 99 percent of its total customers and approximately 91 percent of its net operating revenues as of February 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;For additional information related to rate matters within the Distribution segment, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates &#8211; Missouri Gas Energy </font>and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">New England Gas Company.</font></font></div>

<td valign="bottom" width="120%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(1)</font><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt; COLOR: black">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating revenues for the Distribution segment are reported net of <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Cost of natural gas</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">and other energy</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Revenue-related taxes</font>, which are pass-through costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(2)</font><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt; COLOR: black">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">"Degree days" are a measure of the coldness of the weather experienced.&#160;&#160;A degree day is equivalent to each degree that the daily mean temperature for a day falls below 65 degrees Fahrenheit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Year ended December 31, 2010 versus the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;</font>The $18.1 million loss recorded in 2010 is due to the First Circuit affirming the Company&#8217;s conviction of an RCRA violation in a mercury permitting trial and denying the Company's petition for an <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic">en banc</font> rehearing.&#160;&#160;&#160;See<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> Item 8. <div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Preferred Stock Dividends and Loss on Extinguishment of Preferred Stock</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Year ended December 31, 2010 versus the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>The $348,000 reduction in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Preferred stock dividends</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Loss on extinguishment of preferred stock</font> for the year ended December 31, 2010 versus the same period in 2009 was due to the impact of the loss of $3.3 million the Company recorded in the 2010 period related to its redemption of all of its 4,600,013 depository shares outstanding representing 460,000 shares of its 7.55% Noncumulative Preferred Stock, Series A (Liquidation Preference $250 per share) (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Preferred Stock</font>) and the reduction in related dividends of $3.6 million in the 2010 period versus the 2009 period associated with these redemptions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accelerated First-Year Tax Depreciation.</font>&#160;&#160;As a result of recent federal income tax legislation, bonus depreciation is allowed for the cost of qualified property placed in service after 2007 and before 2014.&#160;&#160;The majority of such qualifying property has historically been depreciated over a seven to fifteen year period.&#160;&#160;The Company has realized an estimated $26 million tax benefit for the years 2008 through 2010 associated with additional first-year bonus tax depreciation in excess of historical tax depreciation.&#160;&#160;The amount of tax benefit applicable to years 2011 through 2013 will be subject to the level of qualified property placed in service during those years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s current business strategy includes making prudent capital expenditures across its base of transmission, storage, gathering, processing and distribution assets and growing the businesses through the selective acquisition of assets in order to position itself favorably in the evolving natural gas markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Cash flows used in investing activities in the year ended December 31, 2010 and 2009 were $392.5 million and $419.4 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The $26.9 million decrease in investing cash outflows was primarily due to a $97.8 million decrease in capital expenditures in the Transportation and Storage segment, partially offset by a $100 million equity contribution the Company made to Citrus to partially fund the Phase VIII Expansion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Principal Capital Expenditure Projects</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 1. Business &#8211; Business Segments &#8211; Transportation and Storage Segment &#8211; Recent System Enhancements &#8211; Completed or Under Construction </font>for additional information on the major 2010 and ongoing capital expenditure projects within the Company&#8217;s Transportation and Storage segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2008 Hurricane Damage.</font>&#160;&#160;In September 2008, Hurricanes Gustav and Ike came ashore on the Louisiana and Texas coasts.&#160;&#160;Damage from the hurricanes affected the Company&#8217;s Transportation and Storage segment.&#160;&#160;Offshore transportation facilities, including Sea Robin and Trunkline, suffered damage to several platforms and gathering pipelines.&#160;&#160;In late July 2009, during testing to put the remaining offshore facilities back in service, Sea Robin experienced a pipeline rupture in an area where the pipeline had previously been displaced during Hurricane Ike and subsequently re-buried.&#160;&#160;Sea Robin experienced reduced volumes until January 2010 when the remainder of the damaged facilities was back in service.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The capital replacement and retirement expenditure estimates relating to Hurricane Ike have been reduced from $185 million to approximately $150 million and are expected to be completed in 2011.&#160;&#160;Approximately $134 million, $110 million and $23 million of the capital replacement and retirement expenditures were incurred as of December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company anticipates reimbursement from OIL for a significant portion of the damages in excess of its $10 million deductible; however, the recoverable amount is subject to pro rata reduction to the extent that the level of total accepted claims from all insureds exceeds the carrier&#8217;s $750 million aggregate exposure limit.&#160;&#160;OIL announced that it has reached the $750 million aggregate exposure limit and currently calculates its estimated payout amount at 70 percent or less based on estimated claim information it has received.&#160;&#160;OIL is currently making interim payouts at the rate of 50 percent of accepted claims.&#160;&#160;The Company received a total of $25.8 million and $36.7 million in 2010 and 2009, respectively, for claims submitted to date with respect to Hurricane Ike.&#160;&#160;The final amount of any applicable pro rata reduction cannot be determined until OIL has received and assessed all claims.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Potential Sea Robin Impairment</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.&#160;&#160;</font>Sea Robin, comprised primarily of offshore facilities, suffered damage from Hurricane Ike related to several platforms and gathering pipelines.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 2 &#8211; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Other Matters &#8211; Asset Impairment</font> for information related to the Company&#8217;s analysis of the Sea Robin assets for potential impairment as of December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;As there were no indicators of potential impairment during 2010, the impairment test on Sea Robin was not performed as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The Company currently estimates that approximately $115 million of the approximately $150 million total estimated capital replacement and retirement expenditures to replace property and equipment damaged by Hurricane Ike are related to Sea Robin.&#160;&#160;The Company anticipates partial reimbursement from its property insurance carrier for its damages in excess of its $10 million deductible, except for certain expenditures not reimbursable under the insurance policy terms.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 14 &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies &#8211; Other Commitments and Contingencies &#8211; 2008 Hurricane Damage </font>for additional related information.&#160;&#160;Additionally, Sea Robin has implemented a rate surcharge approved by FERC in September 2009, subject to refund, to recover Hurricane Ike related costs not otherwise recovered from insurance proceeds or from other third parties.&#160;&#160;To the extent the Company&#8217;s capital expenditures are not recovered through insurance proceeds or through its hurricane rate surcharge, its net investment in Sea Robin&#8217;s property and equipment would increase without necessarily generating additional revenues unless the incremental costs are recovered through future rate proceedings or additional throughput.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates &#8211; Panhandle</font> for information related to the surcharge filing.&#160;&#160;If the amount of the estimated Sea Robin insurance reimbursements are significantly reduced or Sea Robin experiences other adverse developments incrementally impacting the Company&#8217;s related net investment or anticipated future cash flows that are not remedied through rate proceedings, the Company could potentially be required to record an impairment of its net investment in Sea Robin.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Missouri Safety Program.&#160;&#160;</font>Pursuant to a 1989 MPSC order, Missouri Gas Energy is engaged in a major natural gas safety program in its service territories (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Missouri Safety Program</font>).&#160;&#160;This program includes replacement of Company and customer-owned natural gas service and yard lines, the movement and resetting of meters, the replacement of cast iron mains and the replacement and cathodic protection of bare steel mains.&#160;&#160;In recognition of the significant capital expenditures associated with this safety program, the MPSC initially permitted the deferral and subsequent recovery through rates of depreciation expense, property taxes and associated carrying costs over a 10-year period.&#160;&#160;On August 28, 2003, the State of Missouri passed certain statutes that provided Missouri Gas Energy the ability to adjust rates periodically to recover depreciation expense, property taxes and carrying costs associated with the Missouri Safety Program, as well as investments in public improvement projects.&#160;&#160;The continuation of the Missouri Safety Program will result in significant levels of future capital expenditures.&#160;&#160;The Company incurred capital expenditures of $13.6 million in 2010 related to this program and estimates incurring approximately $104.9 million over the next 10 years, after which all service lines, representing about 39 percent of the annual safety program investment, will have been replaced.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Citrus Sponsor Contributions. </font>In 2010, the Company and Citrus&#8217; other shareholder each made a $100 million sponsor capital contribution in the form of equity to Citrus to partially fund the Phase VIII Expansion.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s $100 million capital contribution was funded using its credit facilities.&#160;&#160;During the first half of 2011, it is expected Citrus will require additional sponsor provided contributions, which may be in the form of loans or equity contributions from each of its shareholders of up to $150 million.&#160;&#160;Citrus plans to resume cash distributions, which may be in the form of loan repayments or dividends, to its sponsors after the Phase VIII Expansion project is placed in service.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For additional information related to the Company&#8217;s strategy regarding other growth opportunities, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 7. Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#8211; Business Strategy</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Debt Refinancing, Repayment and Issuance Activity</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">8.125% Senior Notes.&#160; </font>In June 2009, PEPL issued $150 million in senior notes due June 1, 2019 with an interest rate of 8.125 percent (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">8.125% Senior Notes</font>).&#160; In connection with the issuance of the 8.125% Senior Notes, PEPL incurred underwriting and discount costs totaling approximately $1 million, resulting in approximately $149 million in proceeds to PEPL.&#160; These proceeds were used to repay borrowings under the Company&#8217;s credit facilities and to repay the $60.6 million of 6.50% Senior Notes that matured on July 15, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">7.00% Senior Notes.&#160;&#160;</font>In June 2008, PEPL issued $400 million in senior notes due June 15, 2018 with an interest rate of 7.00 percent (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">7.00% Senior Notes</font>).&#160; In connection with the issuance of the 7.00% Senior Notes, PEPL incurred underwriting and discount costs totaling approximately $4.1 million, resulting in approximately $395.9 million in proceeds to PEPL.&#160; These proceeds were advanced to Southern Union and used to repay borrowings under its credit facilities.&#160;&#160;Southern Union repaid PEPL a portion of the advance to retire the $300 million 4.80% Senior Notes in August 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Term Loans.</font>&#160;&#160;On August 5, 2009, the Company entered into a two-year $150 million term loan (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">2009 Term Loan</font>) with a syndicate of banks.&#160;&#160;The proceeds of the 2009 Term Loan were used to repay borrowings under the credit facilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On August 3, 2010, the Company entered into an Amended and Restated $250 million Credit Agreement, maturing on August 3, 2013 (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">2010 Term Loan</font>).&#160;&#160;The 2010 Term Loan bears interest at a rate of LIBOR plus 2.125 percent.&#160;&#160;The 2010 Term Loan amended, restated and upsized the 2009 Term Loan.&#160;&#160;The 2009 Term Loan had an interest rate of LIBOR plus 3.75 percent.&#160;&#160;Proceeds received from the 2010 Term Loan were used to refinance the existing indebtedness under the 2009 Term Loan described above, with the remaining proceeds to be used to provide working capital and for general corporate purposes.&#160;&#160;The balance of the 2010 Term Loan was $250 <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">million with an effective interest rate of 2.39 percent at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The balance and effective interest rate of the Amended Credit Agreement at February 18, 2011 were $250 million and 2.39 percent, respectively.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Credit Facilities.</font>&#160;&#160;On February 26, 2010, the Company entered into the Sixth Amended and Restated Revolving Credit Agreement with the banks named therein in the amount of $550 million (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">2010 Revolver</font>).&#160;&#160;The 2010 Revolver will mature on May 28, 2013.&#160;&#160;Borrowings on the 2010 Revolver are available for the Company&#8217;s working capital, other general corporate purposes and letter of credit requirements.&#160;&#160;The interest rate and commitment fee under the 2010 Revolver are calculated using a pricing grid, which is based upon the credit rating for the Company&#8217;s senior unsecured notes.&#160;&#160;The annualized interest rate and commitment fee rate bases for the 2010 Revolver at December 31, 2010 were LIBOR, plus 275 basis points, and 50 basis points, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s additional $20 million short-term committed credit facility was renewed in July 2010 for an additional 364-day period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2010 Revolver is a refinancing of the Company&#8217;s $400 million Fifth Amended and Restated Revolving Credit Agreement (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Revolver</font>), which was otherwise scheduled to mature on May 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under the Revolver were available for Southern Union&#8217;s working capital and letter of credit requirements and other general corporate purposes.&#160;&#160;The interest rate for the Revolver was based on LIBOR plus 62.5 basis points.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Balances of $297.1 million and $80 million were outstanding under the Company&#8217;s credit facilities at effective interest rates of 3.02 percent and 0.85 percent at December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company classifies its borrowings under the credit facilities as short-term debt, as the individual borrowings are generally for periods of 15 to 180 days.&#160;&#160;At maturity, the Company may (i) retire the outstanding balance of each borrowing with available cash on hand and/or proceeds from a new borrowing, or (ii) at the Company&#8217;s option, extend the borrowing&#8217;s maturity date for up to an additional 90 days.&#160;&#160;As of February 18, 2011, there was a balance of $243.8 million outstanding under the Company&#8217;s credit facilities at an average effective interest rate of 3.03&#160;percent.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Common Stock and Equity Units Issuances</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 8, 2008, the Company remarketed its 4.375% Senior Notes, which yielded no cash proceeds for the Company.&#160;&#160;The interest rate on the Senior Notes was reset to 6.089 percent per annum effective on and after February 19, 2008.&#160;&#160;The 6.089% Senior Notes matured on February 16, 2010.&#160;&#160;On February 19, 2008, the Company issued 3,693,240 shares of common stock for $100 million in cash proceeds in conjunction with the remarketing of the 4.375% Senior Notes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company believes that inflation has caused, and may continue to cause, increases in certain operating expenses, capital replacement and construction costs.&#160;&#160;In the Transportation and Storage and Distribution segments, the Company continually reviews the adequacy of its rates in relation to such increasing cost of providing services, the inherent regulatory lag experienced in adjusting its rates and the rates it is actually able to charge in its markets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Matters Impacting the Company&#8217;s Unconsolidated Investment in Citrus</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Florida Gas and an affiliate of El Paso each submitted a bid in response to Florida Power &amp; Light Company&#8217;s (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">FPL</font>) proposed 300-mile Florida EnergySecure intrastate pipeline project, and FPL entered into a non-binding letter of intent with the El Paso affiliate in connection with such project.&#160;&#160;Although the Florida Public Service Commission did not approve the Florida EnergySecure intrastate pipeline project, FPL has indicated that it may seek bids for a future project.&#160;&#160;El Paso has reasserted that it is entitled to, and communicated that it currently intends that it may, participate in any such bidding process.&#160;&#160;In light of existing circumstances, Florida Gas, Citrus and Southern Union continue to disagree with El Paso&#8217;s position.&#160;&#160;A successful bid on such FPL project by El Paso, if the project ultimately is approved, could adversely impact Florida Gas&#8217; ultimate contract terms for the remaining uncommitted Phase VIII Expansion transportation capacity and Florida Gas&#8217; future growth opportunities in Florida.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 49.65pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Rate Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Trunkline LNG Cost and Revenue Study.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>On July 1, 2009, Trunkline LNG filed a Cost and Revenue Study with respect to the Trunkline LNG facility expansions completed in 2006, in compliance with FERC orders.&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>Such filing, which was as of March 31, 2009, reflected an annualized cost of service level and associated revenues of $54.7 million and $68.5 million, respectively.&#160; BG LNG Services (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">BGLS</font>) filed a motion to intervene and protest on July 14, 2009.&#160; By order dated July 26, 2010, FERC determined that since (i) Trunkline LNG has fixed negotiated rates with BGLS through 2015, which would be unaffected by any rate change that might be determined through hearing at this time, and (ii) current costs and revenues are not necessarily representative of Trunkline LNG&#8217;s costs and revenues at the termination of the negotiated rate period in 2015, there was no reason to expend FERC&#8217;s and the parties&#8217; resources on a Natural Gas Act Section 5 proceeding at this time.&#160; The order is final and not subject to rehearing.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Effects of Regulation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is subject to regulation by certain state and federal authorities in each of its reportable segments.&#160;&#160;Missouri Gas Energy, New England Gas Company and Florida Gas have accounting policies that are in accordance with the accounting requirements and ratemaking practices of the applicable regulatory authorities.&#160;&#160;The application of these accounting policies allows the Company to defer expenses and revenues on the balance sheet as regulatory assets and liabilities when it is probable that those expenses and revenues will be allowed in the ratemaking process in a period different from the period in which they would have been reflected in the Consolidated Statement of Operations by an unregulated company.&#160;&#160;These deferred assets and liabilities then flow through the results of operations in the period in which the same amounts are included in rates and recovered from or refunded to customers.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s assessment of the probability of recovery or pass through of regulatory assets and liabilities requires judgment and interpretation of laws and regulatory commission orders.&#160;&#160;If, for any reason, the Company ceases to meet the criteria for application of regulatory accounting treatment for all or part of its operations, the regulatory assets and liabilities related to those portions ceasing to meet such criteria would be eliminated from the Consolidated Balance Sheet and included in the Consolidated Statement of Operations for the period in which the discontinuance of regulatory accounting treatment occurs.&#160;&#160;The aggregate amount of regulatory assets reflected in the Consolidated Balance Sheet applicable to the Distribution segment are $66.2 million and $72.3 million at December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;The aggregate amount of regulatory liabilities reflected in the Consolidated Balance Sheet applicable to the Distribution segment are $5.8 million and $8.5 million at December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;For a summary of regulatory matters applicable to the Company, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates</font>.&#160;&#160;Panhandle and SUGS do not currently apply regulatory accounting standards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Significant changes to these assumptions or estimates could require a provision for impairment in a future period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Long-Lived Assets Impairment Evaluation.&#160;&#160;</font>An impairment loss is recognized when the carrying amount of a long-lived asset used in operations is not recoverable and exceeds its fair value.&#160;&#160;The carrying amount of a long-lived asset is not recoverable if it exceeds the sum of the undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use and eventual disposition of the asset.&#160;&#160;An impairment loss is measured as the amount by which the carrying amount of a long-lived asset exceeds its fair value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A long-lived asset is tested for recoverability whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that its carrying amount may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;Long-lived assets or asset groups used in operations are evaluated for potential impairment at the lowest level for which identifiable cash flows are largely independent of the cash flows of other groups of assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;A two-step impairment test is performed to identify a potential impairment and measure an impairment loss, if any, to be charged to earnings.&#160;&#160;Step one determines if the carrying amount ascribed to a long-lived asset or asset group is recoverable based on undiscounted cash flows.&#160;&#160;If the asset or asset group fails the step one recoverability test (i.e. related carrying amount is in excess of the undiscounted cash flows), then, as a second step, the fair value of the asset or asset group is compared to the related carrying amount to determine the amount of impairment loss to be charged to earnings.&#160;&#160;The fair value in the second test is primarily determined based upon discounted cash flows associated with the asset or asset group using assumptions that market participants would use.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The long-lived assets of Sea Robin were evaluated as of December 31, 2009 because indicators of potential impairment were evident primarily due to the impacts associated with Hurricanes Gustav and Ike.&#160;&#160;See related information in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 7. Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#8211; Liquidity and Capital Resources &#8211; Investing Activities &#8211; Principal Capital Expenditure Projects &#8211; 2008 Hurricane Damage</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Potential Sea Robin Impairment.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Goodwill Impairment Evaluation.&#160;&#160;</font>At December 31, 2010, the Company had a goodwill balance of $89.2 million relating to its Distribution segment reporting unit.&#160;&#160;The Company assesses goodwill for impairment at least annually as of November 30, and updates the annual test on an interim basis if events or circumstances occur that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of the applicable reporting unit below its book carrying amount.&#160;&#160;A two-step impairment test is performed to identify a potential impairment and measure an impairment loss, if any, to be charged to earnings.&#160;&#160;In the first step, the fair value of the reporting unit, which is primarily determined based on discounted cash flows using assumptions that market participants would use, is compared <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">to the reporting unit&#8217;s carrying amount, including goodwill.&#160;&#160;If the carrying amount of the reporting unit is greater than its fair value, the reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill may be impaired and step two must be completed.&#160;&#160;In the second step, the carrying amount of the reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill is compared with the implied fair value of such goodwill.&#160;&#160;If the carrying amount of the reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill is greater than its implied fair value, an impairment loss must be charged to earnings for the excess (i.e. recorded goodwill must be written down to implied fair value of the reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill).&#160;&#160;Because the fair value of goodwill can be measured only as a residual amount and cannot be determined directly, the implied fair value of a reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill is calculated in the same manner as the amount of goodwill that is recognized in a purchase business combination.&#160;&#160;This process involves measuring the fair value of the reporting unit&#8217;s assets and liabilities (both recognized and unrecognized) at the time of the impairment test by performing a hypothetical purchase price allocation.&#160;&#160;The difference between the reporting unit&#8217;s fair value and the fair values assigned to the reporting unit&#8217;s individual assets and liabilities (both recognized and unrecognized), is the implied fair value of the reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company evaluated goodwill for potential impairment for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, and no impairment was indicated in the step one test.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Equity Method Investments.</font>&#160;&#160;A loss in value of an equity method investment that is other than temporary is recognized in earnings.&#160;&#160;Evidence of a loss in value might include, but would not necessarily be limited to, absence of an ability to recover the carrying amount of the investment or inability of the investee to sustain an earnings capacity that would justify the carrying amount of the investment.&#160;&#160;A current fair value of an investment that is less than its carrying amount may indicate a loss in value of the investment.&#160;&#160;All of the above factors are considered in the Company&#8217;s review of its equity method investments.&#160;&#160;The Company evaluated its equity method investments for potential impairment for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, and no impairment was indicated.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Pensions and Other Postretirement Benefits</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective December 31, 2008, the Company is required to measure plan assets and benefit obligations as of its fiscal year-end balance sheet date. The Company recognizes the changes in the funded status of its defined benefit postretirement plans through <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The calculation of the Company&#8217;s net periodic benefit cost and benefit obligation requires the use of a number of assumptions.&#160;&#160;Changes in these assumptions can have a significant effect on the amounts reported in the financial statements.&#160;&#160;The Company believes that the two most critical assumptions are the assumed discount rate and the expected rate of return on plan assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company establishes the discount rate using the Citigroup Pension Discount Curve as published on the Society of Actuaries website as the hypothetical portfolio of high-quality debt instruments that would provide the necessary cash flows to pay the benefits when due.&#160;&#160;Net periodic benefit cost and the benefit obligation increases and equity correspondingly decreases as the discount rate is reduced.&#160;&#160;Lowering the discount rate assumption by 0.5 percent would increase the Company&#8217;s 2010 net periodic benefit cost (before regulatory accounting adjustments) and benefit obligation at the end of 2010 by approximately $770,000 and $19.1 million, respectively, and would correspondingly increase <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> at the end of 2010 by $19.1 million on a pre-tax basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The expected rate of return on plan assets is based on long-term expectations given current investment objectives and historical results.&#160;&#160;Net periodic benefit cost increases as the expected rate of return on plan assets is correspondingly reduced.&#160;&#160;Lowering the expected rate of return on plan assets assumption by 0.5 percent would increase the Company&#8217;s 2010 net periodic benefit cost (before regulatory accounting adjustments) by approximately $980,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 8 &#8211;</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Benefits</font> for additional related information.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Derivatives and Hedging Activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All derivatives are recognized on the balance sheet at their fair value.&#160;&#160;On the date the derivative contract is entered into, the Company designates the derivative as:&#160;&#160;(i) a hedge of the fair value of a recognized asset or liability or of an unrecognized firm commitment (fair value hedge);&#160;&#160;(ii) a hedge of a forecasted transaction or the variability of cash flows to be received or paid in conjunction with a recognized asset or liability (cash flow hedge); or (iii) an instrument that is held for trading or non-hedging purposes (a trading or economic hedging instrument).&#160;&#160;For derivatives treated as a fair value hedge, the effective portion of changes in fair value is recorded as an adjustment to the hedged item.&#160;&#160;The ineffective portion of a fair value hedge is recognized in earnings if the short cut method of assessing effectiveness is not used.&#160;&#160;Upon termination of a fair value hedge of a debt instrument, the resulting gain or loss is amortized to earnings through the maturity date of the debt instrument.&#160;&#160;For derivatives treated as a cash flow hedge, the effective portion of changes in fair value is recorded in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> until the related hedged items impact earnings.&#160;&#160;Any ineffective portion of a cash flow hedge is reported in current-period earnings.&#160;&#160;For derivatives treated as trading or economic hedging instruments, changes in fair value are reported in current-period earnings.&#160;&#160;Fair value is determined based upon quoted market prices and pricing models using assumptions that market participants would use.&#160;&#160;See the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Fair Value Measurement</font> discussion below for additional information related to the framework used by the Company to measure the fair value of its derivative financial instruments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company formally assesses, both at the hedge&#8217;s inception and on an ongoing basis, whether the derivatives that are used in hedging transactions have been highly effective in offsetting changes in the fair value or cash flows of hedged items and whether those derivatives may be expected to remain highly effective in future periods.&#160;&#160;The Company discontinues hedge accounting when: (i) it determines that the derivative is no longer effective in offsetting changes in the fair value or cash flows of a hedged item; (ii) the derivative expires or is sold, terminated, or exercised; (iii) it is no longer probable that the forecasted transaction will occur; or (iv) management determines that designating the derivative as a hedging instrument is no longer appropriate.&#160;&#160;In all situations in which hedge accounting is discontinued and the derivative remains outstanding, the Company will carry the derivative at its fair value on the balance sheet, recognizing changes in the fair value in current-period earnings.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 10 &#8211; Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value Measurement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&#160;&#160;The Company utilizes market data or assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability, including assumptions about nonperformance risk, which is primarily comprised of credit risk (both the Company&#8217;s own credit risk and counterparty credit risk) and the risks inherent in the inputs to any applicable valuation techniques.&#160;&#160;The Company places more weight on current market information concerning credit risk (e.g. current credit default swap rates) as opposed to historical information (e.g. historical default probabilities and credit ratings).&#160;&#160;These inputs can be readily observable, market corroborated, or generally unobservable.&#160;&#160;The Company endeavors to utilize the best available information, including valuation techniques that maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs.&#160;&#160;The three-tier fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value is as follows:</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method. Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the estimated future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rate is recognized in earnings in the period that includes the enactment date. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the amounts more likely than not to be realized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The determination of the Company&#8217;s provision for income taxes requires significant judgment, use of estimates, and the interpretation and application of complex tax laws. Significant judgment is required in assessing the timing and amounts of deductible and taxable items.&#160;&#160;Reserves are established when, despite management&#8217;s belief that the Company&#8217;s tax return positions are fully supportable, management believes that certain positions may be successfully challenged. When facts and circumstances change, these reserves are adjusted through the provision for income taxes.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 9 &#8211; Taxes on Income </font>for additional related information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commitments and Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Note 2 &#8211; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Other Matters &#8211; New Accounting Principles</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM 7A.&#160;&#160;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Interest Rate Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is subject to the risk of loss associated with movements in market interest rates.&#160;&#160;The Company manages this risk through the use of fixed-rate debt, floating-rate debt and interest rate swaps.&#160;&#160;Fixed-rate swaps are used to reduce the risk of increased interest costs during periods of rising interest rates.&#160;&#160;Floating-rate swaps are used to convert the fixed rates of long-term borrowings into short-term variable rates.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the interest rate on 83 percent of the Company&#8217;s long-term debt was fixed after considering the impact of interest rate swaps.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2010, $19.7 million is included in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Derivative instruments - liabilities</font> and $4.6 million is included in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Deferred Credits</font> in the Consolidated Balance Sheet related to the fixed-rate interest rate swaps on the $455 million Term Loan due 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2010, a 100 basis point change in the annual interest rate on all outstanding floating-rate long- and short-term debt would correspondingly change the Company&#8217;s interest payments by approximately $800,000 for each month during which such change continued.&#160;&#160;If interest rates changed significantly, the Company may take actions to manage its exposure to the change.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company has entered into treasury rate locks from time to time to manage its exposure against changes in future interest payments attributable to changes in the US treasury rates.&#160;&#160;By entering into these agreements, the Company locks in an agreed upon interest rate until the settlement of the contract, which typically occurs when the associated long-term debt is sold.&#160;&#160;The Company accounts for the treasury rate locks as cash flow hedges.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s most recent treasury rate locks were settled in February and June 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The change in exposure to loss in earnings and cash flow related to interest rate risk for the year ended December 31, 2010 is not material to the Company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font>,<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> Note 10 &#8211; Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</font> and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 7 </font>- <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Debt Obligations</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commodity Price Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gathering and Processing Segment.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company markets natural gas and NGL in its Gathering and Processing segment and manages associated commodity price risks using both economic and accounting hedge derivative financial instruments.&#160;&#160;These instruments involve not only the risk of transacting with counterparties and their ability to meet the terms of the contracts, but also the risks associated with unmatched positions and market fluctuations.&#160;&#160;The Company is required to record its commodity derivative financial instruments at fair value, which is affected by commodity exchange prices, over-the-counter quotes, volatility, time value, credit and counterparty credit risk and the potential impact on market prices of liquidating positions in an orderly manner over a reasonable period of time under current market conditions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To manage its commodity price risk related to natural gas and NGL, the Company may use a combination of (i) natural gas puts, price swaps and basis swaps, (ii) NGL processing spread puts and swaps, and (iii) other exchange-traded futures and options.&#160;&#160;These derivative financial instruments allow the Company to preserve value and protect margins.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2010, excluding the effects of hedging and assuming normal operating conditions, the Company estimates that a change in price of $0.01 per gallon of NGL and $1.00 per MMBtu of natural gas would impact annual gross margin by approximately $1.5 million and $7.4 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Such commodity price risk estimates do not include any effect on demand for the Company&#8217;s services that may be caused by, or arise in conjunction with, price changes.&#160;&#160;For example, a change in the gross processing spread may cause some ethane to be sold in the natural gas stream, impacting gathering and processing margins, natural gas deliveries and NGL volumes shipped.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Transportation and Storage Segment.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font> The Company is exposed to some commodity price risk with respect to natural gas used in operations by its interstate pipelines.&#160;&#160;Specifically, the pipelines receive natural gas from customers for use in generating compression to move the customers&#8217; natural gas.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the pipelines may have to settle system imbalances when customers&#8217; actual receipts and deliveries do not match.&#160;&#160;When the amount of natural gas utilized in operations by the pipelines differs from the amounts provided by customers, the&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">pipelines may use natural gas from inventory or may have to buy or sell natural gas to cover these or other operational needs, resulting in commodity price risk exposure to the Company.&#160;&#160;In addition, there is other indirect exposure to the extent commodity price changes affect customer demand for and utilization of transportation and storage services provided by the Company.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, there were no hedges in place with respect to natural gas price risk associated with the Company&#8217;s interstate pipeline operations.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution Segment Economic Hedging Activities.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company enters into financial instruments to mitigate price volatility of purchased natural gas passed through to customers in the Distribution segment. The cost of the derivative products and the settlement of the respective obligations are recorded through the natural gas purchase adjustment clause as authorized by the applicable regulatory authority and therefore do not impact earnings. The fair values of the contracts are recorded as an adjustment to a regulatory asset or liability in the Consolidated Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the fair values of the contracts, which expire at various times through December 2012, are included in the Consolidated Balance Sheet as liabilities, with matching adjustments to deferred cost of natural gas of $37.4 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">1.&#160;&#160;Corporate Structure</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 1932.&#160;&#160;The Company owns and operates assets in the regulated and unregulated natural gas industry and is primarily engaged in the gathering, processing, transportation, storage and distribution of natural gas in the United States.&#160;&#160;Through Panhandle, the Company owns and operates approximately 10,000 miles of interstate pipelines that transport up to 5.5 Bcf/d of natural gas from the Gulf of Mexico, South Texas and the Panhandle regions of Texas and Oklahoma to major U.S. markets in the Midwest and Great Lakes regions.&#160;&#160;Panhandle also owns and operates an LNG import terminal located on Louisiana&#8217;s Gulf Coast.&#160;&#160;Through its investment in Citrus, the Company has an interest in and operates Florida Gas, an interstate pipeline company that transports natural gas from producing areas in South Texas through the Gulf Coast region to Florida.&#160;&#160;Through SUGS<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">, </font>the Company owns approximately 5,500 miles of natural gas and NGL pipelines, four cryogenic plants with a combined capacity of 415 MMcf/d and five natural gas treating plants with combined capacities of 585 MMcf/d.&#160;&#160;SUGS is primarily engaged in connecting wells of natural gas producers to its gathering system, treating natural gas to remove impurities to meet pipeline quality specifications, processing natural gas for the removal of NGL, and redelivering natural gas and NGL to a variety of markets.&#160;&#160;Its operations are located in West Texas and Southeast New Mexico.&#160;&#160;Through Southern Union&#8217;s regulated utility operations, Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company, the Company serves natural gas end-user customers in Missouri and Massachusetts, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2.&#160;&#160;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Other Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Basis of Presentation.</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with GAAP.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Principles of Consolidation.</font>&#160;&#160;The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Southern Union and its wholly-owned subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Investments in which the Company has significant influence over the operations of the investee are accounted for using the equity method.&#160;&#160;All sig&#173;nifi&#173;cant intercompany accounts and transactions are eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;Certain reclassifications have been made to prior years' financial statements to conform to the current year presentation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of Estimates.</font>&#160;&#160;The preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Property, Plant and Equipment.</font>&#160;&#160;Ongoing additions of property, plant and equipment are stated at cost. The Company capitalizes all construction-related direct labor and material costs, as well as indirect construction costs. The cost of replacements and betterments that extend the useful life of property, plant and equipment is also capitalized. The cost of repairs and replacements of minor property, plant and equipment items is charged to expense as incurred.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When property, plant and equipment is retired within the Company&#8217;s Transportation and Storage and Distribution segments, the original cost less salvage value is charged to accumulated depreciation and amortization.&#160;&#160;When entire regulated operating units of property, plant and equipment are retired or sold or non-regulated properties are retired or sold, the property and related accumulated depreciation and amortization accounts are reduced, and any gain or loss is recorded in earnings.&#160;&#160;When property, plant and equipment is retired within the Company&#8217;s Gathering and Processing segment, the original cost less salvage value and accumulated depreciation and amortization balances are removed, with the resulting gain or loss recorded in earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company computes depreciation expense using the straight-line method.&#160;&#160;Depreciation rates for the utility plants are approved by the applicable regulatory commissions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Computer software, which is a component of property, plant and equipment, is stated at cost and is generally amortized on a straight-line basis over its useful life on a product-by-product basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For additional information, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 12 &#8211; Property, Plant and Equipment</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Asset Impairment.</font>&#160;&#160;An impairment loss is recognized when the carrying amount of a long-lived asset used in operations is not recoverable and exceeds its fair value.&#160;&#160;The carrying amount of a long-lived asset is not recoverable if it exceeds the sum of the undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use and eventual disposition of the asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A long-lived asset is tested for recoverability whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that its carrying amount may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;The long-lived assets of Sea Robin were evaluated as of December 31, 2009 because indicators of potential impairment were evident primarily due to the impacts associated with Hurricane Ike and due to reductions in the estimated payout from the Company&#8217;s insurance carrier for reimbursable expenditures for the repair, retirement or replacement of the Company&#8217;s property, plant and equipment damaged by Hurricane Ike, which is more fully discussed in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 14 &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies &#8211; Other Commitments and Contingencies &#8211; 2008 Hurricane Damage</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As there were no indicators of potential impairment during 2010, the impairment test on Sea Robin was not performed as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;However, to the extent the Company&#8217;s capital expenditures resulting from Hurricane Ike damage are not recovered through insurance proceeds or through Sea Robin&#8217;s hurricane rate surcharge, its net investment in Sea Robin&#8217;s property and equipment will have increased without necessarily realizing corresponding cash inflows unless the incremental costs are recovered through future rate proceedings or additional throughput.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates &#8211; Sea Robin</font> for information related to the surcharge filing.&#160;&#160;If the surcharge filing is not ultimately approved by FERC or Sea Robin experiences other adverse developments incrementally impacting the Company&#8217;s related net investment or anticipated future cash flows that are not remedied through rate proceedings, the Company could potentially be required to record an impairment of its net investment in Sea Robin.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Goodwill.</font>&#160;&#160;Goodwill resulting from a purchase business combination is not amortized, but instead is tested for impairment at the Company&#8217;s Distribution segment reporting unit level at least annually by applying a fair-value based test.&#160;&#160;The annual impairment test is updated if events or circumstances occur that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of the reporting unit below its book carrying value.&#160;&#160;The Company evaluated goodwill for potential impairment for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, and no impairment was indicated in the step one test.&#160;&#160;There were no changes recorded to goodwill for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash and Cash Equivalents.</font>&#160;&#160;Cash equivalents consist of highly liquid investments, which are readily convertible into cash and have original maturities of three months or less.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the Company&#8217;s cash management system, checks issued but not presented to banks frequently result in book overdraft balances for accounting purposes and are classified in accounts payable in the Consolidated Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010 and 2009, such book overdraft balances classified in accounts payable were approximately $12 million and $26.2 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Segment Reporting.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company reports its operations under three reportable segments: the Transportation and Storage segment, the Gathering and Processing segment and the Distribution segment.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 17 &#8211; Reportable Segments </font>for additional related information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
