<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Interest Rate Contracts</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company enters into interest rate swaps to manage its exposure to changes in interest payments on long-term debt attributable to movements in market interest rates, and enters into treasury rate locks to manage its exposure to changes in future interest payments attributable to changes in treasury rates prior to the issuance of new long-term debt instruments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Interest Rate Swaps.</font>&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Company had outstanding pay-fixed interest rate swaps with a total notional amount of $455 million applicable to the LNG Holdings $455 million term loan issued in 2007.&#160;&#160;These interest rate swaps are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the effective portion of changes in their fair value recorded in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> and reclassified into <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Interest expense</font> in the same periods during which the related interest payments on long-term debt impact earnings.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, approximately $11.8 million of net after-tax losses in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> related to these interest rate swaps is expected to be amortized into <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Interest expense</font> during the next twelve months.&#160;&#160;Any ineffective portion of the cash flow hedge is reported in current-period earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Treasury Rate Locks.</font>&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Company had no outstanding treasury rate locks.&#160;&#160;However, certain of its treasury rate locks that settled in prior periods are associated with interest payments on outstanding long-term debt.&#160;&#160;These treasury rate locks are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the effective portion of their settled value recorded in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> and reclassified into <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Interest expense</font> in the same periods during which the related interest payments on long-term debt impact earnings.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, approximately $571,000 of net after-tax losses in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss </font>related to these treasury rate locks will be amortized into <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Interest expense</font> during the next twelve months.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commodity Contracts &#8211; Gathering and Processing Segment</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company primarily enters into natural gas price swaps and NGL processing spread swaps to manage its exposure to changes in margin on forecasted sales of natural gas and NGL volumes resulting from movements in market commodity prices.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas Price Swaps</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font>&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Company had outstanding receive-fixed natural gas price swaps with a total notional amount of 9,125,000 MMBtus for 2011.&#160;&#160;&#160;These natural gas price swaps are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the effective portion of changes in their fair value recorded in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> and reclassified into <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Operating revenues</font> in the same periods during which the forecasted natural gas sales impact earnings.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, approximately $10.5 million of net after-tax gains in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</font> related to these natural gas price swaps is expected to be amortized into <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Operating revenues</font> during the next twelve months.&#160;&#160;Any ineffective portion of the cash flow hedge is reported in current-period earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NGL Processing Spread Swaps</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">.</font>&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the Company had outstanding receive-fixed NGL processing spread swaps with a total notional amount of 9,125,000 MMBtu equivalents for 2011.&#160;&#160;These processing spread swaps are accounted for as economic hedges, with changes in their fair value recorded in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Operating revenues</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commodity Contracts - Distribution Segment</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company enters into natural gas commodity financial instruments to manage the exposure to changes in the cost of natural gas passed through to utility customers that result from movements in market commodity prices.&#160;&#160;The cost of the derivative instruments and settlement of the respective obligations are recovered from utility customers through the purchased natural gas adjustment clause as authorized by the applicable regulatory authority and therefore do not impact earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain of the Company&#8217;s derivative instruments contain provisions that require the Company&#8217;s debt to be maintained at an investment grade credit rating from each of the major credit rating agencies.&#160;&#160;If the Company&#8217;s debt were to fall below investment grade, the Company would be in violation of these provisions, and the counterparties to the derivative instruments could potentially require the Company to post collateral for certain of the derivative instruments.&#160;&#160;The aggregate fair value of all derivative instruments with credit-risk-related contingent features that are in a net liability position at December 31, 2010 was $29.7 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Amortization expense of capitalized computer software costs for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008 was $11.4 million, $13.1 million and $12.1 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Computer software costs are amortized between one and fifteen years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">13.&#160;&#160;Stock-Based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair value of each stock option and SAR award is estimated on the date of grant using a Black-Scholes option pricing model. The Company&#8217;s expected volatilities are based on historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock.&#160;&#160;To the extent that volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock price increases in the future, the estimates of the fair value of stock options and SARs granted in the future could increase, thereby increasing share-based compensation expense in future periods.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the expected dividend yield is considered for each grant on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s expected term of stock options and SARs granted was derived from the average midpoint between vesting and the contractual term.&#160;&#160;In the future, as information regarding post-vesting termination becomes more accessible, the Company may change the method of deriving the expected term.&#160;&#160;This change could impact the fair value of stock options and SARs granted in the future.&#160;&#160;The risk-free rate is based on the U.S.&#160;Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of grant.</font></div>

That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average contractual period of 2.31 years. The total fair value of options and SARs vested as of December 31, 2010 was $16.9 million. Compensation expense recognized related to stock options and SARs totaled $6.3 million ($4.0 million, net of tax), $5.4 million ($3.5 million, net of tax) and $3.9 million ($2.7 million, net of tax) for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;Cash received from the exercise of stock options was $1.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The intrinsic value of options and SARs exercised during the year ended December 31, 2010 was approximately $581,000.&#160;&#160;The Company realized an additional tax benefit of approximately $276,000 for the excess amount of deductions related to stock options and SARs over the historical book compensation expense multiplied by the statutory tax rate in effect, which has been reported as an increase in financing cash flows in the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s Third Amended 2003 Plan also provides for grants of restricted stock equity units, which are settled in shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, and restricted stock liability units, which are settled in cash.&#160;&#160;The restrictions associated with a grant of restricted stock equity units under the Third Amended 2003 Plan generally expire equally over a period of three years.&#160;&#160;Restrictions on certain grants made to non-employee directors and senior executives of the Company expire over a shorter time period, in certain cases less than one year, and may be subject to accelerated expiration over a shorter term if certain criteria are met.&#160;&#160;The restrictions associated with a grant of restricted stock liability units expire equally over a period of three years and are payable in cash at the vesting date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2010, there was $16.3 million of total unrecognized compensation cost related to non-expired, restricted stock equity units and restricted stock liability units compensation arrangements granted under the restricted stock plans. That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average contractual period of 2.13&#160;years. The total fair value of restricted stock equity and liability units that were released during the year ended December 31, 2010 was $8.4 million. Compensation expense recognized related to restricted stock equity <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">and liability units totaled $8.8 million ($5.5 million, net of tax), $6.8 million ($4.3 million, net of tax) and $3.7 million ($2.3 million, net of tax) for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font> </font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">14.&#160;&#160;Commitments and Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Environmental</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s operations are subject to federal, state and local laws and regulations regarding water quality, hazardous and solid waste management, air quality control and other environmental matters. These laws and regulations require the Company to conduct its operations in a specified manner and to obtain and comply with a wide variety of environmental registrations, licenses, permits, inspections and other approvals.&#160;&#160;Failure to comply with environmental requirements may expose the Company to significant fines, penalties and/or interruptions in operations. The Company&#8217;s environmental policies and procedures are designed to achieve compliance with such laws and regulations. These evolving laws and regulations and claims for damages to property, employees, other persons and the environment resulting from current or past operations may result in significant expenditures and liabilities in the future. The Company engages in a process of updating and revising its procedures for the ongoing evaluation of its operations to identify potential environmental exposures and enhance compliance with regulatory requirements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is allowed to recover environmental remediation expenditures through rates in certain jurisdictions within its Distribution segment. Although significant charges to earnings could be required prior to rate recovery for jurisdictions that do not have rate recovery mechanisms, management does not believe that environmental expenditures will have a material adverse effect on the Company's consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The table below reflects the amount of accrued liabilities recorded in the Consolidated Balance Sheet at the dates indicated to cover probable environmental response actions.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, the Company had $4.5 million, $12 million and $12&#160;million of expenditures related to environmental cleanup programs, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SPCC Rules.</font>&#160;&#160;In October 2007, the EPA proposed amendments to the SPCC rules with the stated intention of providing greater clarity, tailoring requirements and streamlining requirements.&#160;&#160;On October 7, 2010, EPA amended the compliance date for certain facilities from November 10, 2010 to November 10, 2011.&#160;&#160;The Company is currently reviewing the impact of the modified regulations on its operations in its Transportation and Storage and Gathering and Processing segments and may incur costs for tank integrity testing, alarms and other associated corrective actions as well as potential upgrades to containment structures.&#160;&#160;Costs associated with such activities cannot be estimated with certainty at this time, but the Company believes such costs will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Air Quality Control. </font>In August 2010, EPA finalized a rule that requires reductions in a number of pollutants, including formaldehyde and carbon monoxide, for certain engines regardless of size at Area Sources (sources that emit less than ten tons per year of any one Hazardous Air Pollutant (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">HAP</font>) or twenty-five tons per year of all HAPs) and engines less than 500 horsepower at Major Sources (sources that emit ten tons per year or more of any one HAP or twenty-five tons per year of all HAPs).&#160;&#160;Compliance is required by October 2013.&#160;&#160;It is anticipated that the limits adopted in this rule will be used in a future EPA rule that is scheduled to be finalized in 2013, with compliance required in 2016.&#160;&#160;This future rule is expected to require reductions in formaldehyde and carbon monoxide emissions from engines greater than 500 horsepower at Major Sources.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Nitrogen oxides are the primary air pollutant from natural gas-fired engines.&#160;&#160;Nitrogen oxide emissions may form ozone in the atmosphere.&#160;&#160;EPA lowered the ozone standard to seventy-five parts per billion (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">ppb</font>) in 2008 with compliance anticipated in 2013 to 2015.&#160;&#160;In January 2010, EPA proposed lowering the standard to sixty to seventy ppb in lieu of the seventy-five ppb standard, with compliance required in 2014 or later.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In January 2010, EPA finalized a 100 ppb one-hour nitrogen dioxide standard.&#160;&#160;The rule requires the installation of new nitrogen dioxide monitors in urban communities and roadways by 2013.&#160;&#160;This new network may result in additional nitrogen dioxide non-attainment areas.&#160;&#160;In addition, ambient air quality modeling may be required to demonstrate compliance with the new standard.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is currently reviewing the potential impact of the August 2010 Area Source National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants rule and proposed rules regarding HAPs and ozone and the new nitrogen dioxide standard on operations in its Transportation and Storage and Gathering and Processing segments and the potential costs associated with the installation of emission control systems on its existing engines.&#160;&#160;Costs associated with these activities cannot be estimated with any certainty at this time, but the Company believes such costs will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Transportation and Storage Segment Environmental Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas Transmission Systems.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>Panhandle is responsible for environmental remediation at certain sites on its natural gas transmission systems for contamination resulting from the past use of lubricants containing PCBs in compressed air systems; the past use of paints containing PCBs; and the prior use of wastewater collection facilities and other on-site disposal areas. Panhandle has developed and implemented a program to remediate such contamination.&#160;&#160;The primary remaining remediation activity on the Panhandle systems is associated with past use of paints containing PCBs or PCB impacts to equipment surfaces and to a building at one location.&#160;&#160;The PCB assessments are ongoing and the related estimated remediation costs are subject to further change.&#160;&#160;The Company believes the total PCB remediation costs will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other remediation typically involves the management of contaminated soils and may involve remediation of groundwater. Activities vary with site conditions and locations, the extent and nature of the contamination, remedial requirements, complexity and sharing of responsibility.&#160;&#160;The ultimate liability and total costs associated with these sites will depend upon many factors. If remediation activities involve statutory joint and several liability provisions, strict liability, or cost recovery or contribution actions, Panhandle could potentially be held responsible for contamination caused by other parties. In some instances, Panhandle may share liability associated with contamination with other PRPs.&#160;&#160;Panhandle may also benefit from contractual indemnities that cover some or all of the cleanup costs. These sites are generally managed in the normal course of business or operations.&#160;&#160;The Company believes the outcome of these matters will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Air Quality Control.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>The Kansas Department of Health and Environment set certain contingency measures as part of the agency&#8217;s ozone maintenance plan for the Kansas City area.&#160;&#160;These measures must be revised to conform to the requirements of the EPA ozone standard discussed above.&#160;&#160;As such, the costs associated with these activities cannot be estimated with any certainty at this time, but the Company believes such costs will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 18, 2009, PEPL received an information request from the EPA under Section 114(a) of the Federal Clean Air Act.&#160; The information request sought certain documents and records pertaining to maintenance activities and capital projects associated with combustion emission sources located at eight compressor stations in Illinois and Indiana. &#160;The complete responses were provided in February 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gathering and Processing Segment Environmental Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Gathering and Processing Systems.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>SUGS is responsible for environmental remediation at certain sites on its gathering and processing systems, resulting primarily from releases of hydrocarbons.&#160;&#160;SUGS has a program to remediate such contamination.&#160;&#160;The remediation typically involves the management of contaminated soils and may involve remediation of groundwater. Activities vary with site conditions and locations, the extent and nature of the contamination, remedial requirements and complexity.&#160;&#160;The ultimate liability and total costs associated with these sites will depend upon many factors. These sites are generally managed in the normal course of business or operations. The Company believes the outcome of these matters will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Air Quality Control.</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>SUGS is currently negotiating settlements to certain enforcement actions by the NMED and the TCEQ.&#160;&#160;The Company believes the outcome of these matters will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution Segment Environmental Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is responsible for environmental remediation at various contaminated sites that are primarily associated with former MGPs and sites associated with the operation and disposal activities of former MGPs that produced a fuel known as &#8220;town gas&#8221;. Some byproducts of the historic manufactured gas process may be regulated substances under various federal and state environmental laws. To the extent these byproducts are present in soil or groundwater at concentrations in excess of applicable standards, investigation and remediation may be required.&#160;&#160;The sites include properties that are part of the Company&#8217;s ongoing operations, sites formerly owned or used by the Company and sites owned by third parties. Remediation typically involves the management of contaminated soils and may involve removal of old MGP structures and remediation of groundwater. Activities vary with site conditions and locations, the extent and nature of the contamination, remedial requirements, complexity and sharing of responsibility; some contamination may be unrelated to former MGPs. The ultimate liability and total costs associated with these sites will depend upon many factors. If remediation activities involve statutory joint and several liability provisions, strict liability, or cost recovery or contribution actions, the Company could potentially be held responsible for contamination caused by other parties.&#160;&#160;In some instances, the Company may share liability associated with contamination with other PRPs and may also benefit from insurance policies or contractual indemnities that cover some or all of the cleanup costs. These sites are generally managed in the normal course of business or operations. The Company believes the outcome of these matters will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">North Attleboro MGP Site in Massachusetts (North Attleboro Site).</font>&#160;&#160;In November 2003, the MADEP issued a Notice of Responsibility to New England Gas Company, acknowledging receipt of prior notifications and investigative reports submitted by New England Gas Company, following the discovery of suspected coal tar material at the North Attleboro Site.&#160;&#160;Subsequent sampling in the adjacent river channel revealed sediment impacts necessitating the investigation of off-site properties.&#160;&#160;Assessment activities continue at the remaining areas on-site and at the off-site properties.&#160;&#160;It is estimated that the Company will spend approximately $9.6 million over the next several years to complete the investigation and remediation activities at the North Attleboro Site, as well as maintain the engineered barrier constructed in 2008 at the upland portion of the site.&#160;&#160;As New England Gas Company is allowed to recover environmental remediation expenditures through rates associated with its Massachusetts operations, the estimated costs associated with the North Attleboro Site have been included in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Regulatory assets</font> in the Consolidated Balance Sheet.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Litigation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company is involved in legal, tax and regulatory proceedings before various courts, regulatory commissions and governmental agencies regarding matters arising in the ordinary course of business, some of which involve substantial amounts.&#160;&#160;Where appropriate, the Company has established reserves in order to provide for such matters.&#160;&#160;The Company believes the final disposition of these proceedings will not have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mercury Release</font>. In October 2004, New England Gas Company discovered that one of its facilities, formerly associated with discontinued operations which were sold in 2006, had been broken into and that mercury had been released both inside a building and in the immediate vicinity, including a parking lot in a neighborhood several blocks away. Mercury from the parking lot was apparently tracked into nearby apartment units, as well as other buildings. Cleanup was completed at the property and nearby apartment units. The vandals who broke into the facility were arrested and convicted. In October 2007, the U.S. Attorney in Rhode Island filed a three-count indictment against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic">District Court</font>) alleging violation of permitting requirements under the federal RCRA and notification requirements under the federal Emergency Planning and Community Right to Know Act (EPCRA) relating to the 2004 incident. Trial commenced on September 22, 2008, and on October 15, 2008, the jury acquitted Southern Union on the EPCRA count and one of the two RCRA counts and found the Company guilty on the other RCRA count. On October 2, 2009, the District Court imposed a fine of $6 million and a payment of $12 million in community service. The Court stayed the payment of the fine and community service amounts while the Company pursued an appeal of the conviction and sentence to the United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic">First Circuit</font>).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 22, 2010, a First Circuit panel affirmed the conviction and the sentence. On February 17, 2011, the First Circuit denied the Company&#8217;s petition for <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">en banc</font> rehearing.&#160;&#160;The Company now intends to petition for a writ of certiorari review by the United States Supreme Court.&#160;&#160;The Government has agreed to stay enforcement of the sentence, including payment of the fine and community service, pending resolution of the Company's petition to the United States Supreme Court.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">With regard to the sentence, the First Circuit panel ruled that although the jury&#8217;s verdict was necessarily limited to a single day&#8217;s violation of RCRA (carrying a maximum fine of $50,000), the trial judge was nevertheless authorized for sentencing purposes independently to find the number of days the Company purportedly violated RCRA.&#160;&#160;In its decision, the Panel noted that the sentencing issue as applied to criminal fines was a novel one in the First Circuit and that, if the First Circuit panel's application of judicial precedents is incorrect, it would not be harmless error to the Company and the case must be remanded to the District Court for resentencing.&#160;&#160;In its petition for rehearing &#8220;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">en banc</font>&#8221; by the full First Circuit, the Company argued that the conviction violated the Company&#8217;s due process rights, and that the sentence, which went beyond the fine authorized by the jury&#8217;s verdict, violated the Company&#8217;s jury trial rights under the Sixth Amendment, and is contrary to current Supreme Court precedent and the decisions of two other federal circuits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In light of the First Circuit's decisions, the Company recorded a charge to earnings of approximately $18.1 million and reported such charge as Loss&#160;from discontinued operations in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. The earnings charge is nondeductible for federal and state income tax purposes, resulting in a reduction in the Company's basic and fully diluted EPS for 2010 of $0.14 and $0.14, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Will Price.</font>&#160;&#160;Will Price, an individual, filed actions in the U.S. District Court for the District of Kansas for damages against a number of companies, including Panhandle, alleging mis-measurement of natural gas volumes and Btu content, resulting in lower royalties to mineral interest owners.&#160;&#160;On September 19, 2009, the Court denied <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">plaintiffs&#8217; request for class certification.&#160;&#160;Plaintiffs have filed a motion for reconsideration, which the Court denied on March 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Panhandle believes that its measurement practices conformed to the terms of its FERC natural gas tariffs, which were filed with and approved by FERC.&#160;&#160;As a result, the Company believes that it has meritorious defenses to the Will Price lawsuit (including FERC-related affirmative defenses, such as the filed rate/tariff doctrine, the primary/exclusive jurisdiction of FERC, and the defense that Panhandle complied with the terms of its tariffs).&#160;&#160;In the event that Plaintiffs refuse Panhandle&#8217;s pending request for voluntary dismissal, Panhandle will continue to vigorously defend the case.&#160;&#160;The Company does not believe the outcome of the Will Price litigation will have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">East End Project.</font>&#160; The East End project involved the installation of a total of approximately 31 miles of pipeline in and around Tuscola, Illinois, Montezuma, Indiana and Zionsville, Indiana.&#160;&#160;Construction began in 2007 and was completed in the second quarter of 2008.&#160;&#160;PEPL is seeking recovery of each contractor&#8217;s share of approximately $50 million of cost overruns from the construction contractor, an inspection contractor and the construction management contractor for improper welding, inspection and construction management of the East End Project.&#160;&#160;Certain of the contractors have filed counterclaims against PEPL for alleged underpayments of approximately $18 million.&#160;&#160;The matter is pending in state court in Harris County, Texas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The trial date is currently set for May 2011.&#160;&#160;The Company does not believe the outcome of this case will have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Commitments and Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Retirement of Debt Obligations.</font>&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 7 &#8211; Debt Obligations &#8211; Retirement of Debt Obligations </font>for information related to the Company&#8217;s debt maturing in 2011. &#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2008 Hurricane Damage.</font>&#160;&#160;In September 2008, Hurricanes Gustav and Ike came ashore on the Louisiana and Texas coasts.&#160;&#160;Damage from the hurricanes affected the Company&#8217;s Transportation and Storage segment.&#160;&#160;Offshore transportation facilities, including Sea Robin and Trunkline&#8217;s Terrebonne system, suffered damage to several platforms and gathering pipelines.&#160;&#160;In late July 2009, during testing to put the remaining offshore facilities back in service, Sea Robin experienced a pipeline rupture in an area where the pipeline had previously been displaced during Hurricane Ike and subsequently re-buried.&#160;&#160;Sea Robin experienced reduced volumes until January 2010 when the remainder of the damaged facilities was placed back in service.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2010, the Company recorded a reduction in Hurricane Ike related expenses of approximately $8.1 million and insurance recoveries of $4.1 million.&#160;&#160;The Company had previously recorded Hurricane Ike related expenses of approximately $12.3 million and $10.5 million, and insurance recoveries of $2.1 million and nil, in 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;The capital replacement and retirement expenditure estimates relating to Hurricane Ike have been reduced from $185 million to approximately $150 million and are expected to be completed in 2011.&#160;&#160;Approximately $134 million, $110 million and $23 million of the capital replacement and retirement expenditures were incurred as of December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company anticipates reimbursement from OIL for a significant portion of the damages in excess of its $10 million deductible; however, the recoverable amount is subject to pro rata reduction to the extent that the level of total accepted claims from all insureds exceeds the carrier&#8217;s $750 million aggregate exposure limit.&#160;&#160;OIL announced that it has reached the $750 million aggregate exposure limit and currently calculates its estimated payout amount at 70 percent or less based on estimated claim information it has received.&#160;&#160;OIL is currently making interim payouts at the rate of 50 percent of accepted claims.&#160;&#160;The Company received a total of $25.8 million and $36.7 million in 2010 and 2009, respectively, for claims submitted to date with respect to Hurricane Ike.&#160;&#160;The final amount of any applicable pro rata reduction cannot be determined until OIL has received and assessed all claims.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Purchase Commitments.&#160;&#160;</font>At December 31, 2010, the Company had purchase commitments for natural gas transportation services, storage services and certain quantities of natural gas at a combination of fixed, variable and market-based prices that have an aggregate value of approximately $652 million.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s purchase commitments may be extended over several years depending upon when the required quantity is purchased.&#160;&#160;The Company has purchased natural gas tariffs in effect for all its utility service areas that provide for recovery of its purchased natural gas costs under defined methodologies and the Company believes that all costs incurred under such commitments will be recovered through its purchased natural gas tariffs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Missouri Safety Program.&#160;&#160;</font>Pursuant to a 1989 MPSC order, Missouri Gas Energy is engaged in its service territories in the Missouri Safety Program.&#160;&#160;This program includes replacement of Company and customer-owned natural gas service and yard lines, the movement and resetting of meters, the replacement of cast iron mains and the replacement and cathodic protection of bare steel mains.&#160;&#160;In recognition of the significant capital expenditures associated with this safety program, the MPSC initially permitted the deferral and subsequent recovery through rates of depreciation expense, property taxes and associated carrying costs over a 10-year period.&#160;&#160;On August 28, 2003, the State of Missouri passed certain statutes that provided Missouri Gas Energy the ability to adjust rates periodically to recover depreciation expense, property taxes and carrying costs associated with the Missouri Safety Program, as well as investments in public improvement projects.&#160;&#160;The continuation of the Missouri Safety Program will result in significant levels of future capital expenditures.&#160;&#160;The Company incurred capital expenditures of $13.6 million in 2010 related to this program and estimates incurring approximately $104.9 million over the next 10 years, after which all service lines, representing about 39 percent of the annual safety program investment, will have been replaced.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation and Rates.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 18 &#8211; Regulation and Rates </font>for potential contingent matters associated with the Company&#8217;s regulated operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock Award Plans.</font>&#160;&#160;The Third Amended 2003 Plan allows for awards in the form of stock options (either incentive stock options or non-qualified options), SARs, stock bonus awards, restricted stock, performance units or other equity-based rights.&#160;&#160;The persons eligible to receive awards under the Third Amended 2003 Plan include all of the employees, directors, officers and agents of, and other service providers to, the Company and its affiliates and subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Under the Third Amended 2003 Plan: (i) no participant may receive in any calendar year awards covering more than 500,000 shares; (ii) the exercise price for a stock option may not be less than 100 percent of the fair market value of the common stock on the date of grant; and (iii) no award may be granted after September 28, 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company maintains its 1992 Plan, under which options to purchase 8,491,540 shares of its common stock were authorized to be granted until July 1, 2002 to officers and key employees.&#160;&#160;Options granted under the 1992 Plan are exercisable for ten years from the date of grant or such lesser period as may be designated for particular options, and became exercisable after a specified period of time from the date of grant in cumulative annual installments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For more information on share-based awards, see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 13 &#8211; Stock-Based Compensation</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">16.&#160;&#160;Preferred Securities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 8, 2003, the Company issued 9,200,000 depositary shares, each representing a 1/10<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font> interest in a share of its 7.55% Noncumulative Preferred Stock, Series A (Liquidation Preference $250 Per Share) (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Preferred Stock</font>), at the public offering price of $25 per share, or $230 million in the aggregate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May 22, 2008, the Company announced that the finance committee of its Board had authorized a program to repurchase a portion of the depositary shares representing ownership of its Preferred Stock at the Company&#8217;s discretion in the open market and/or through privately negotiated transactions, subject to market conditions, applicable legal requirements and other factors.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2008, the Company paid $115.2 million to repurchase 4,599,987 depository shares representing 459,999 shares of Preferred Stock, resulting in a $3.5 million non-cash loss adjustment charged to <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Retained earnings</font> related to the write-off of issuance costs, which reduced <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net earnings available for common stockholders</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July 30, 2010, the Company redeemed the remaining approximately 460,000 shares of outstanding Preferred Stock at $25 per share, which totaled $115 million.&#160;&#160;The Company recognized a $3.3 million non-cash loss adjustment charged to <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Retained earnings</font> related to the write-off of issuance costs that reduced <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net earnings available for common stockholders</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">17.&#160;&#160;Reportable Segments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company&#8217;s reportable business segments are organized based on the way internal managerial reporting presents the results of the Company&#8217;s various businesses to its executive management for use in determining the performance of the businesses and in allocating resources to the businesses, as well as based on similarities in economic characteristics, products and services, types of customers, methods of distribution and regulatory environment.&#160;&#160;The Company operates in three reportable segments:&#160;&#160;Transportation and Storage, Gathering and Processing, and Distribution.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Transportation and Storage segment operations are conducted through Panhandle and the Company&#8217;s investment in Citrus.&#160;&#160;The Gathering and Processing segment operations are conducted through SUGS.&#160;&#160;The Distribution segment is primarily engaged in the local distribution of natural gas in Missouri and Massachusetts, through its Missouri Gas Energy and New England Gas Company operating divisions, respectively.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Note 1 &#8211; Corporate Structure </font>for additional information associated with the Company&#8217;s reportable segments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The remainder of the Company&#8217;s business operations, which do not meet the quantitative threshold for segment reporting, are presented as Corporate and other activities.&#160;&#160;Corporate and other activities consist of unallocated corporate costs, a wholly-owned subsidiary with ownership interests in electric power plants, and other miscellaneous activities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Company evaluates operational and financial segment performance based on several factors, of which the primary financial measure is EBIT, a non-GAAP measure.&#160;&#160;The Company defines EBIT as <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net earnings available for common stockholders</font>, adjusted for the following:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>

<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">items that do not impact net earnings, such as extraordinary items, discontinued operations and the impact of changes in accounting principles;</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>

</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">18.&#160;&#160;Regulation and Rates</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Panhandle.</font>&#160;&#160;Trunkline LNG commenced construction of an enhancement at its LNG terminal in February 2007.&#160;&#160;The key components of the enhancement are an ambient air vaporizer system and NGL recovery units.&#160;&#160;On March 11, 2010, Trunkline LNG received approval from FERC to place the infrastructure enhancement construction project in service.&#160;&#160;Total construction costs were approximately $440 million plus capitalized interest, which includes additional costs incurred during final commissioning.&#160;&#160;The negotiated rate with the project&#8217;s customer, BG LNG Services, will be adjusted based on final capital costs pursuant to a contract-based formula.&#160;&#160;In addition, Trunkline LNG and BG LNG Services have extended the existing terminal and pipeline services agreements to coincide with the infrastructure enhancement construction project contract, which runs 20 years from the in-service date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On August 31, 2009, Sea Robin filed with FERC to implement a rate surcharge to recover Hurricane Ike-related costs not otherwise recovered from insurance proceeds or from other third parties, with initial accumulated net costs of approximately $38 million included in the filing.&#160; On September 30, 2009, FERC approved the surcharge to be effective March 1, 2010, subject to refund and the outcome of hearings with FERC to explore issues set <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">forth in certain customer protests, including the costs to be included and the applicability of the surcharge to discounted contracts.&#160; On August 31, 2010, Sea Robin submitted its semiannual filing related to the surcharge which reflected updated costs incurred of approximately $46 million, net of insurance and surcharge recoveries, which were reflected in the updated surcharge rate effective October 1, 2010, subject to refund.&#160;&#160;The Administrative Law Judge issued an initial decision on December 13, 2010, approving the surcharge for recovery from all shippers, including discounted and non-discounted shippers, over a recovery period of 21.4 years and including applicable carrying charges.&#160;&#160;The Company, as well as other parties, have filed briefs for exception on certain aspects of the decision.&#160;&#160;The ultimate outcome of this matter is pending a final FERC decision.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">F-58</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SOUTHERN UNION COMPANY AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 15, 2003, the U.S. Department of Transportation issued a final rule requiring pipeline operators to develop integrity management programs to comprehensively evaluate their pipelines, and take measures to protect pipeline segments located in what the rule defines as HCAs. This rule resulted from the enactment of the Pipeline Safety Improvement Act of 2002. The rule requires operators to identify HCAs along their pipelines and to complete baseline integrity assessments, comprised of in-line inspection (smart pigging), hydrostatic testing or direct assessment, by December 2012. Operators were required to rank the risk of their pipeline segments containing HCAs, assessments are generally conducted on the higher risk segments first.&#160; In addition, some system modifications will be necessary to accommodate the in-line inspections. As of December 31, 2010, the Company had completed approximately 90 percent of the baseline risk assessments required to be completed by December 2012. While identification and location of all the HCAs has been completed, it is not practicable to determine with certainty the total scope of required remediation activities prior to completion of the assessments and inspections. The required modifications and inspections are currently estimated to be in the range of approximately $10 million to $20 million per year through 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Missouri Gas Energy.&#160;&#160;</font>On April 2, 2009, Missouri Gas Energy made a filing with the MPSC seeking to implement an annual base rate increase of approximately $32.4 million.&#160;&#160;On February 10, 2010, the MPSC issued its Report and Order in this case, authorizing a revenue increase of $16.2 million and approving distribution rate structures for Missouri Gas Energy&#8217;s residential and small general service customers (which comprised approximately 99 percent of its total customers and approximately 91 percent of its net operating revenues at the time the rates went into effect) that eliminate the impact of weather and conservation for residential and small general service margin revenues and related earnings in Missouri.&#160;&#160;The new rates became effective February 28, 2010.&#160;&#160;Judicial review of the MPSC&#8217;s Report and Order is being sought by the Office of the Public Counsel, with respect to rate structure issues, and by Missouri Gas Energy, with respect to cost of capital issues.&#160;&#160;Those judicial review proceedings are not expected to be complete until 2011, and the results of those judicial review proceedings are not expected to have a material adverse impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">New England Gas Company.</font>&#160;&#160;On September 16, 2010, New England Gas Company made a filing with the MDPU seeking to implement an annual base rate increase of approximately $6.2 million.&#160; The filing includes a proposed implementation of a revenue decoupling mechanism, which mitigates conservation and weather impacts.&#160;&#160;The filing also includes a proposed Targeted Infrastructure Replacement Factor, which will permit recovery of capital costs associated with certain aged facilities without the requirement to make a filing with the MDPU to request an increase in the annual base rate.&#160;&#160;New rates are expected to become effective April 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;On October 8, 2010, the MDPU issued an order seeking comments as to the appropriateness of dismissing New England Gas Company&#8217;s pending rate case filing as a result of certain concerns related to a MDPU required audit of New England Gas Company for 2007.&#160; The MDPU has not made a ruling with regard to the potential dismissal of New England Gas Company&#8217;s pending rate case filing.&#160;&#160;New England Gas Company believes that neither the facts nor the law support or permit the issuance of a dismissal order and would, in the event of its issuance, vigorously contest any such dismissal order.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 15, 2008, New England Gas Company made a filing with the MDPU seeking recovery of approximately $4 million, or 50 percent of the amount by which its 2007 earnings fell below a return on equity of 7 percent.&#160;&#160;This filing was made pursuant to New England Gas Company&#8217;s rate settlement approved by the MDPU </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">in 2007.&#160;&#160;On February 2, 2009, the MDPU issued its order denying the Company&#8217;s requested earnings sharing adjustments (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">ESA</font>) in its entirety.&#160;&#160;The Company appealed that decision to the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MSJC</font>) on February 17, 2009.&#160;&#160;On November 13, 2009, New England Gas Company made a similar filing with the MDPU, also pursuant to the above-referenced settlement, to recover approximately $1.7 million, representing 50 percent of the amount by which its 2008 earnings deficiency fell below a return on equity of 7 percent.&#160;&#160;The MDPU held the 2008 ESA matter in abeyance pending judicial resolution of the issues pertaining to the 2007 ESA.&#160;&#160;On February 11, 2011, the MSJC issued an opinion reversing the MDPU&#8217;s rejection of New England Gas Company&#8217;s 2007 ESA and remanded the matter back to the MDPU to determine the appropriate amount of the 2007 ESA and the method for recovery.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><br>
&#160;</div>
